ak.name: Alaska

early.text: Early and absentee in-person voting started Oct 19 (15 days before) and runs through Election Day. Hours and which ballots are available depend on the location.

mail.text: Anyone can vote by mail, no reason needed. The deadline to request a mail ballot was Oct 24 (online-delivery and fax ballots can still be requested until 5 p.m. Mon, Nov 2). A mailed ballot counts if it is postmarked by Nov 3 and arrives within 10 days (Nov 13) when mailed from inside the U.S. You can also drop it at any voting location by 8 p.m. on Election Day.

registration.text: The deadline to register was Oct 4, so it has passed. There is no Election Day registration for this election; same-day registration only applies to the presidential race in presidential years. If you registered by Oct 4, you can vote.

ak.note: Confirmed on the Division's pages today: polls 7 a.m.-8 p.m.; early/absentee in-person voting starts 15 days before; no excuse needed; mail-ballot application deadline Oct 24; ballot deadline shown as 'Postmarked or Received by Nov 3'; in-person drop-off by 8 p.m. Election Day. The Nov 13 receipt date (10 days after Election Day for ballots mailed inside the U.S.) comes from the Division's 2026 General media packet via the Oct 19 research; the media packet PDF and the Division's post-election FAQ could not be re-opened today (file download / human-verification page), so Nov 13 and the 'no same-day registration' line are carried over, not re-checked. Ballots mailed from outside the U.S. have 15 days (Nov 18). The Division recommends asking a post office clerk to hand-cancel your envelope so the postmark is dated Nov 3 or earlier. Oct 4 was a Sunday; the Oct 19 file notes regional offices were open for registration Oct 3 and Oct 4.

al.name: Alabama
al.pollHours: 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. (Central time; polling places in Eastern-time areas may use 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Eastern)

early.text: Alabama has no early voting period. You vote at your polling place on Election Day, or you vote by absentee ballot if you have a qualifying reason.

mail.text: You need a reason to vote absentee, and you must list it on your application. A mailed ballot must arrive at your county absentee office by noon on Election Day, Nov. 3. A postmark does not count. You can also hand-deliver it to the office by the close of business (no later than 5 p.m.) on Monday, Nov. 2.

registration.text: The deadline to register to vote in this election was Monday, Oct. 19, 2026. It has passed. Alabama does not have same-day registration.

al.note: Absentee application deadlines: Tue, Oct. 27 if mailed (must be received by then), Thu, Oct. 29 if handed in in person. Voters need a valid photo ID, including for absentee voting. Qualifying reasons include being out of the county on Election Day, illness or disability, working a shift of 10 hours or more that overlaps poll hours, and others listed on the SOS absentee page.

ar.name: Arkansas

early.text: Early voting starts Monday, Oct. 19. Hours are 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Monday to Friday and 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. on Saturday. It ends at 5 p.m. on Monday, Nov. 2. There is no Sunday voting. Locations are set by each county.

mail.text: You need a reason to vote absentee. A mailed ballot must reach your county clerk by 7:30 p.m. on Election Day, Nov. 3. A postmark does not count. If you or a designated helper deliver it in person, it is due by the close of business on Friday, Oct. 30.

registration.text: The deadline to register was Monday, Oct. 5, 2026 (30 days before the election, moved off the Sunday). It has passed. The state calendar lists no same-day registration.

ar.note: The state election calendar PDF I used is the June 2025 revision. The Secretary of State pages do not say outright that same-day registration does not exist, but the calendar gives a firm 30-day deadline and lists no exception. Absentee reasons: out of the area on Election Day, illness or disability, active-duty military (or spouse or dependent), or living outside the U.S. Mail applications were due 7 days before the election (Tue, Oct. 27). A voter's authorized agent can turn in an application until 1:30 p.m. on Election Day. Voters should check the county clerk for early voting sites.

az.name: Arizona

early.text: In-person early voting began Oct 7 and ends Fri, Oct 30. Emergency early voting is available from 7 p.m. Oct 30 to 5 p.m. Mon, Nov 2; ask your County Recorder. Sites and hours are set by each county.

mail.text: Any registered voter can vote early by mail, no reason needed, but the usual request deadline (Oct 23) has passed unless you are already on the Active Early Voting List. A mailed ballot must be received by 7 p.m. on Nov 3 and postmarks do not count. The state says to mail it back by 5 p.m. Tue, Oct 27 (7 days before); after that, drop it at a ballot drop box, early voting site, or your county recorder's office, or at any voting location in your county on Election Day.

registration.text: The deadline to register was Oct 5, so it has passed. Arizona has no Election Day registration. If you are already registered, you can still vote.

az.note: Confirmed today on azsos.gov / arizona.vote: registration deadline Oct 5, early voting begins Oct 7, polls 6 a.m.-7 p.m. (in line by 7 p.m. can vote), ballots must be received by 7 p.m. Election Day, mail back by 5 p.m. seven days before (Oct 27) or use drop-off options. The Oct 30 end of early voting, the emergency voting window, and the Oct 23 request date are carried over from the Oct 19 research (azsos.gov calendar / 2026 publicity pamphlet). Maricopa County and Pima County run their own polling-place finders (locations.maricopa.vote, pima.vote); the state portal covers everyone else. Voter trap: tomorrow (Oct 27) is the state's last recommended mail-back day.

ca.name: California

early.text: Early voting at county elections offices opens Oct. 5. Many counties open more vote centers on Oct. 24, and every county has at least one early location for about the last 10 days. Look up places and hours on the state early voting site.

mail.text: Every active registered voter is mailed a ballot. If you mail it back, it must be postmarked on or before Election Day, Nov. 3, and arrive by Nov. 10. Mail it at least a week early if you can. You can also use a drop box or drop it at a polling place or county elections office by 8 p.m. on Election Day.

registration.sameDayText: From Oct. 20 through Election Day you can 'conditionally' register and vote. Go to your county elections office, a vote center, or a polling place. You vote a provisional ballot, and it is counted once your registration is checked.
registration.text: The regular deadline to register was Monday, Oct. 19, 2026. If you missed it, you can still register and vote using conditional (same-day) registration.

ca.note: A mail ballot dropped in a mailbox on Election Day may get no postmark that day. The state says to take it to a post office counter and ask for a hand postmark, or use a drop box. State pages give slightly different early-voting starts: county election offices Oct. 5, Voter's Choice Act vote centers Oct. 24, and statewide in-person locations by Oct. 31. Check your county for exact sites and hours. Inactive voters are not automatically mailed a ballot.

co.name: Colorado

early.text: Voter service centers are open for in-person voting starting Oct. 19 (some counties open earlier) and stay open through Election Day. Hours vary by county, so check your county on GoVoteColorado.

mail.text: Every active voter is mailed a ballot. Your ballot must be in a drop box, at a voter center, or received by your county clerk by 7 p.m. on Election Day, Nov. 3. A postmark does not count. The state says mail it back by Oct. 26. After that, use a drop box or voter center.

registration.sameDayText: After Oct. 26, you can still register and vote in person at a voter service center, up to 7 p.m. on Election Day.
registration.text: Register by Monday, Oct. 26, 2026 to get a ballot in the mail. After that you can still register and vote in person at a voter center through Election Day.

co.note: Today (Oct. 26) is the state's last suggested day to mail a ballot back, so most voters should now use a drop box or voter center. Voters who get a notice about a signature or ID problem can fix it until Nov. 12. Early voting end date is the day before Election Day; voter centers are also open on Election Day.

ct.name: Connecticut

early.text: Early voting runs 14 days, Oct. 19 to Nov. 1, including both weekends. Most days are 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. On Tue, Oct. 27 and Thu, Oct. 29, hours are 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. You vote at your own town's early voting site.

mail.text: Any registered voter can vote absentee with no reason needed. You must request a ballot by Nov. 2. A mailed or drop-box ballot must reach your town clerk by 8 p.m. on Election Day, Nov. 3. If you bring it yourself, hand it to your town clerk by the close of business on Mon, Nov. 2.

registration.sameDayText: After Oct. 16 you can register and vote in person during early voting (Oct. 19 to Nov. 1) or on Election Day at your town's designated same-day registration spot.
registration.text: The regular deadline to register was Friday, Oct. 16, 2026. After that, use same-day registration in person.

ct.note: Same-day registration on Election Day happens at one designated location in each town, which may not be your usual polling place. A voter's designee (for an ill or disabled voter) can deliver a ballot to the town clerk until 8 p.m. on Election Day. I could not open the myvote.ct.gov page itself; its address comes from the official voter guide.

dc.name: District of Columbia

early.text: Early voting runs Oct. 26 to Nov. 1 at 25 vote centers, every day from 8:30 a.m. to 7 p.m. You can use any of them, no matter where you live in D.C.

mail.text: Every active registered voter is mailed a ballot. A mailed ballot must be postmarked by Nov. 3 and arrive by Fri, Nov. 13. You can also use one of the 55 mail ballot drop boxes (open until 8 p.m. on Election Day) or any vote center.

registration.sameDayText: Same-day registration is available at every early voting and Election Day vote center, with proof of residence.
registration.text: The deadline to register by mail or online was Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026. After that you can still register and vote at a vote center with proof of residence.

dc.note: On Election Day there are 75 vote centers and you can be in line at 8 p.m. and still vote. The USPS does not always postmark mail the day it picks it up, so DCBOE says to mail early or ask for a hand-stamped postmark. D.C. uses ranked-choice voting for some races, which can take longer at the polls.

de.name: Delaware

early.text: Early voting is Oct. 22 to Nov. 1. There is no early voting on Sunday, Oct. 25. Hours are 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. through Tue, Oct. 27, then 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. from Wed, Oct. 28 to Sun, Nov. 1. You can use any early voting site in your county.

mail.text: You need a reason allowed by state law to vote absentee. Your ballot must reach your county Department of Elections office by 8 p.m. on Election Day, Nov. 3. A postmark does not count. Early voting sites and polling places do not accept absentee ballots.

registration.text: The deadline to register was Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. It has passed. Delaware does not offer same-day registration.

de.note: The state's page says the last day to request an absentee ballot to be mailed is Fri, Oct. 30, and the Department must issue absentee ballots by noon on Mon, Nov. 2. With the 8 p.m. receipt deadline, voters should use the county office drop-off instead of mail now. Delaware pages do not explicitly say 'no same-day registration,' but the registration page treats Oct. 10 as the cutoff (in-person office signup was allowed that day only). Early voting is open on Sunday, Nov. 1 but closed on Sunday, Oct. 25.

fl.name: Florida
fl.pollHours: 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. local time (anyone in line at 7 p.m. can vote)

early.text: Every county must offer early voting Oct 24 to Oct 31. Some counties add days between Oct 19 and Oct 23 and/or on Sun, Nov 1, so check your county. Each site is open at least 8 and at most 12 hours a day.

mail.text: No reason is required to vote by mail, but the deadline to ask for a mailed ballot was 5 p.m. Thu, Oct 22. Your ballot must be received by your county Supervisor of Elections by 7 p.m. local time on Nov 3; postmarks do not count. You can hand-deliver it or use a secure drop box at the elections office or early voting sites (until 7 p.m. Election Day).

registration.text: The deadline to register was Oct 5, so it has passed. Florida has no Election Day registration. If you are already registered, you can still vote.

fl.note: State pages confirmed today: request due 5 p.m. on the 12th day before (Oct 22); ballot received by 7 p.m. local time; postmark not enough (only overseas voters get an extension); mandatory early voting from the 10th day before (Oct 24) through the 3rd day before (Oct 31); optional days from the 15th day before (Oct 19) to the 2nd day before (Nov 1); polls 7 a.m.-7 p.m. Picking up a ballot in person after the request deadline requires an emergency affidavit. Part of Florida is in the Central time zone, so 7 p.m. is local time. The Oct 22 request date was also in the Oct 19 file (calendar PDF).

ga.name: Georgia
ga.pollHours: 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. (anyone in line at 7 p.m. can vote)

early.text: In-person advance voting runs Tue, Oct 13 through Fri, Oct 30, including Saturdays Oct 17 and Oct 24. Some counties also open on Sundays (Oct 18 and/or Oct 25). You can use any early voting site in your county.

mail.text: Any voter can vote absentee without a reason, but the deadline to request a ballot was Fri, Oct 23. Your ballot must be received by your county elections office by 7 p.m. on Nov 3; a postmark does not count. You can mail it or put it in a county ballot drop box, so check your county for locations.

registration.text: The deadline to register was Oct 5, so it has passed. Georgia has no Election Day registration. If you are already registered, you can still vote.

ga.note: Confirmed today on sos.ga.gov: last registration day Oct 5, advance voting Oct 13-30, absentee request last day Oct 23, polls 7 a.m.-7 p.m. The Nov 3 7 p.m. receipt deadline and the Sunday/Saturday details are carried over from the Oct 19 research (State Election Board / calendar / Voting in Georgia guide). Advance voting starts Oct 13 because Mon, Oct 12 is a state holiday. Military and overseas ballots postmarked by Election Day count if received within three business days afterward. A photo ID is required to vote in person.

hi.name: Hawaii
hi.pollHours: 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. at voter service centers on Election Day (Hawaii votes mainly by mail and has no neighborhood polling places)

early.text: Voter service centers are open Oct. 20 to Nov. 2, Monday to Saturday, usually 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. They are also open on Election Day, 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Some small-island sites have shorter schedules.

mail.text: Every registered voter is mailed a ballot. It must reach your County Elections Division by 7 p.m. on Election Day, Nov. 3. A postmark does not count. Use a drop box (open from Oct. 14 until 7 p.m. on Election Day) or a voter service center.

registration.sameDayText: You can register and vote in person at any voter service center from Oct. 20 through Election Day.
registration.text: Paper applications must reach your County Elections Division by Monday, Oct. 26, 2026 (4:30 p.m.). You can register online any time. After the deadline you can register and vote at a voter service center.

hi.note: Do not mail your ballot now. It must arrive by 7 p.m. on Nov. 3, so use a drop box or voter service center. Same-day registration is in person at voter service centers, and online registration stays open. Hours and sites differ by county and island.

ia.name: Iowa

early.text: In-person absentee voting at your county auditor's office runs Wed, Oct 14 through Mon, Nov 2. Offices must be open at least 8 hours on Sat, Oct 31; the Nov 2 closing time depends on your auditor.

mail.text: Any registered voter can vote absentee, no excuse needed, but the deadline to request a mailed ballot was 5 p.m. Mon, Oct 19. A returned ballot must be in your county auditor's hands by 8 p.m. on Nov 3, so a postmark does not help. You can hand it to your county auditor any time up to 8 p.m. on Election Day, but you cannot drop it at your polling place.

registration.sameDayText: You can register and vote on Election Day at your assigned polling place. Bring proof of who you are and where you live (an Iowa driver's license with your current address is the easiest), or have someone from your precinct vouch for you.
registration.text: The advance deadline to register was Oct 19, but you can still register and vote on Election Day at your polling place with ID and proof of where you live.

ia.note: Confirmed today on sos.iowa.gov: Election Day registration with ID and proof of residence; absentee request is a written application received by the county auditor 5 p.m. 15 days before (Oct 19); ballots must arrive by 8 p.m. CT on Election Day; voted absentee ballots cannot be delivered to a polling place. Polls 7 a.m.-8 p.m. CT per voterready.iowa.gov and Iowa Code 49.73 (search result; the 9 p.m. closing seen on an older special-election page is outdated). The Oct 14 to Nov 2 in-person absentee window and the Oct 31 Saturday rule are carried over from the Oct 19 research (SOS candidate's guide). Voter trap: if you already have an absentee ballot, you cannot take it to your polling place; you must return it to the county auditor or surrender it at the polls to vote there.

id.name: Idaho
id.pollHours: 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. local time (Idaho has two time zones)

early.text: Early voting (also called in-person absentee) ends Friday, Oct. 30 in every county. Start dates differ: Oct. 13, 14, or 19 depending on your county. Hours and places are set by your county clerk.

mail.text: Any registered voter can ask for an absentee ballot, but the request deadline was 5 p.m. on Oct. 23, so mail ballots are no longer available for most voters. Your voted ballot must reach your county clerk by 8 p.m. on Election Day, Nov. 3. A postmark does not count. Use a drop box or the clerk's office.

registration.sameDayText: You can register in person during early voting (through Oct. 30) or at your polling place on Election Day. Be ready to show a photo ID.
registration.text: Online and mail registration closed at 5 p.m. on Oct. 23, 2026. After that you can still register in person at early voting or on Election Day.

id.note: There is no single statewide early voting start date (Oct. 13, 14, or 19 by county), so start is null. The state says to be ready to show a photo ID; I did not find an official page listing the exact proof-of-residence items for Election Day registration. Online registration and absentee requests both closed at 5 p.m. on Oct. 23. Check your county clerk for early voting hours and places.

il.name: Illinois

early.text: Anyone can vote early in person with no reason needed, through Monday, Nov. 2. Places, hours and start dates are set by your local election authority (many start in September or October). Use the state's early voting location search.

mail.text: Any registered voter can vote by mail with no reason. A mailed ballot must be postmarked by Election Day, Nov. 3, and arrive within 14 days (by Nov. 17). A request sent by mail must reach your election office by Oct. 29. You can also use a drop box if your county has one, before the polls close on Election Day.

registration.sameDayText: Illinois has 'grace period' registration. From Oct. 7 through Election Day you can register and vote in person at your election authority's office or other designated sites, including some polling places on Election Day. Bring two forms of ID, one with your current address. You must have lived in your precinct for 30 days.
registration.text: The regular deadline to register was Tuesday, Oct. 6, 2026 (28 days before the election). After that, use grace period registration in person.

il.note: The state web server blocks automated tools, so I read the State Board of Elections pages and fact sheets through the built-in browser. The Oct. 6 regular registration deadline is calculated from the fact sheet's '28 days before the election' rule, not a printed date. The Nov. 17 receipt date is calculated from the fact sheet's 'within 14 days of Election Day' rule. Postmarks are not guaranteed to be stamped the same day, so the state suggests asking for a hand postmark at a post office counter. Early voting start dates vary by local election authority, so start is null.

in.name: Indiana

early.text: You can vote early in person from Oct. 6 until noon on Monday, Nov. 2. Your county sets the exact places and hours, but every county must be open on the two Saturdays before Election Day (Oct. 24 and Oct. 31).

mail.text: To vote by mail in Indiana you need one of the reasons on the state list, such as being 65 or older, having a disability, or being away all day on Election Day. The time to ask for a mail ballot ended Oct. 22. If you already have one, it must reach your county election office by 6 p.m. on Nov. 3. A postmark does not count.

registration.text: The deadline to register to vote in this election was Oct. 5, 2026. Indiana does not offer same-day registration.

in.note: Mail ballots need an approved reason, and the request deadline (Oct. 22) has passed. Only voters who are confined or caring for a confined person can still ask for a ballot to be delivered, with a request due by noon on Nov. 2. Indiana's state calendar says it reflects Indiana law as of July 2025. Early voting hours differ by county.

ks.name: Kansas
ks.pollHours: 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. local time (counties may open as early as 6 a.m. and close as late as 8 p.m.)

early.text: Kansas calls early voting "advance voting." Counties may start as early as Oct. 14 and every county must be open by Oct. 27. It ends at noon on Monday, Nov. 2. Show a photo ID. Check your county election office for places and hours.

mail.text: Any voter can vote by mail in Kansas, but you must apply for an advance ballot. Kansas law says your ballot must reach the county election office by the time polls close on Nov. 3. You can also drop it in any drop box in your county or hand it in at any polling place in your county before polls close.

registration.text: The deadline to register to vote in this election was Oct. 13, 2026 (21 days before the election). Kansas does not list same-day registration.

ks.note: Mail ballot receipt is confusing. State law and the state's 2026 calendar say mail ballots must arrive by close of polls on Election Day (the old 3-day grace period ended). But the Secretary of State's advance voting page also says a Douglas County court order requires ballots postmarked by Election Day to be counted if they arrive by the last mail delivery on Friday, Nov. 6, and that the state's request to pause that order for the General Election was denied. Because the rules conflict, tell voters to get ballots back by 7 p.m. on Nov. 3. I could not find an official last day to request an advance mail ballot, so it is left out; voters should call their county office right away. Poll hours come from a state page that says to confirm hours with your county.

ky.name: Kentucky

early.text: Any voter can vote early in person on Thursday, Oct. 29, Friday, Oct. 30, and Saturday, Oct. 31. Your county sets the places and hours. Voters with an approved excuse could also vote in person Oct. 21 to 23 and Oct. 26 to 28.

mail.text: Kentucky mail ballots need a qualifying reason, and the time to request one ended Oct. 20. A mail ballot already in your hands must arrive by 6 p.m. local time on Nov. 3. Each county has drop boxes, and the state tells voters not to wait until Election Day to hand-deliver.

registration.text: The deadline to register to vote in this election was Oct. 5, 2026. Kentucky does not offer same-day registration.

ky.note: Early voting for everyone is only three days (Oct. 29 to 31). Mail voting needs an excuse (such as being out of the county, age, disability, or illness), and the request portal closed Oct. 20. The state's page says the Postal Service suggested mailing by Oct. 27, so use a drop box or hand-deliver if you have not mailed yet. An older FAQ page on the same site has different dates; the General Election Summary page was used.

la.name: Louisiana

early.text: Early voting is Oct. 20 to 27, except Sunday, Oct. 25, from 8:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. at your parish registrar of voters office and other set places. Bring a photo ID or be ready to sign an affidavit.

mail.text: Louisiana mail ballots need a qualifying reason, such as age 65 or older, a disability, or being away. The last day to request one is Oct. 30 by 4:30 p.m., and it must reach your parish registrar by 4:30 p.m. on Monday, Nov. 2 (the day before Election Day). Military and overseas voters have until 8 p.m. on Election Day.

registration.text: The deadline to register online was Oct. 13, 2026. The deadline to register in person or by mail was Oct. 5, 2026. Louisiana does not offer same-day registration.

la.note: The mail ballot deadline is the day BEFORE Election Day (Nov. 2, 4:30 p.m.), which surprises people. If you registered online or by mail and have not voted in your parish before, you must vote in person the first time. The state's calendar says Nov. 3 is a U.S. Senate general election and an open primary for U.S. House, with a Dec. 12 general election listed after it, so some House races may not be settled on Nov. 3. The calendar says dates are subject to change by the Legislature.

ma.name: Massachusetts
ma.pollHours: 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. (some towns open earlier; anyone in line at 8 p.m. can vote)

early.text: Early voting runs Oct. 17 through Friday, Oct. 30, with weekend hours in every city and town. Anyone can vote early, no reason needed. Your town sets the places and hours, and many have few or no hours on Fridays.

mail.text: Anyone can vote by mail in Massachusetts. Your application must reach your local election office by 5 p.m. on Tuesday, Oct. 27. Mailed ballots postmarked by Nov. 3 can arrive up to 3 days later (by Nov. 6). You can also use a ballot drop box or hand it in at your local election office; you cannot drop it off at a polling place on Election Day.

registration.text: The deadline to register to vote in this election was Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026 (online until 11:59 p.m., in person until 5 p.m., by mail if postmarked that day). Massachusetts does not offer same-day registration.

ma.note: Mail ballot applications are due tomorrow (Oct. 27, 5 p.m.) and must be at the local office by then, not just mailed. The state says that if you have not mailed your ballot within a week of Election Day, use a drop box or hand it in. The state's Information for Voters page does not mention the Nov. 6 grace period; the Voting by Mail page does. The Nov. 6 arrival date applies only to ballots returned by mail; ballots delivered by hand or drop box must be in by the close of polls on Nov. 3.

md.name: Maryland

early.text: Early voting runs Thursday, Oct. 22 through Thursday, Oct. 29, including the weekend, from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. every day. You vote at an early voting center in the county where you live. Anyone in line at 8 p.m. can vote.

mail.text: Any registered voter can vote by mail in Maryland. Mail your ballot so it is postmarked by Nov. 3, and it counts if your local election office gets it by 10 a.m. on Nov. 13. Or put it in a ballot drop box or hand it in by 8 p.m. on Nov. 3. To get a ballot by mail or fax, your request must arrive by Oct. 27 (online delivery request by Oct. 30).

registration.sameDayText: You can register and vote on the same day at an early voting center (in your county) or at your assigned Election Day polling place. Bring a document that proves where you live.
registration.text: The deadline to register online or by mail was Oct. 13, 2026. After that, you can still register in person during early voting or on Election Day.

md.note: On Election Day you must vote at your assigned polling place (not any location). The state warns that dropping a ballot in a mailbox on Election Day may not get that day's postmark, and says to use a drop box instead. The Nov. 13 10 a.m. arrival date is from the State Board's 2026 election calendar; the public voter pages only say the ballot must be postmarked by Election Day. The mail-fax request deadline of Oct. 27 is tomorrow.

me.name: Maine
me.pollHours: Opens between 6 a.m. and 10 a.m. depending on your town (ask your town office); all polls close at 8 p.m.

early.text: You can vote absentee in person at your town or city clerk's office until close of business Thu, Oct 29. Hours depend on your town, so call first.

mail.text: Anyone can vote absentee, no reason needed. Request your ballot by close of business Thu, Oct 29 (the Thursday before Election Day), but the post office advises asking at least 15 days ahead if you rely on mail. Your clerk must receive the ballot by 8 p.m. on Nov 3; postmarks do not count. The state says mail it by Oct 27 to be safe, or drop it at your town office or its drop box by 8 p.m. on Election Day.

registration.sameDayText: You can register in person at your town or city office or at the polls up until the polls close on Election Day, with proof of who you are and where you live.
registration.text: The deadline to register online or by mail was Oct 13, but you can still register in person through Election Day, including at your polling place.

me.note: Confirmed today on maine.gov/sos: polls open 6-10 a.m. by town and close at 8 p.m.; registration in person until close of polls, online/mail by Oct 13 (online 5 p.m.); absentee request and in-person clerk voting deadline is close of business the Thursday before the election (Oct 29); ballots must be received by 8 p.m. Election Day; USPS advice to request by 15 days and return by 7 days before. Early in-person start is null: the state says ballots are available 30 days before (Oct 4, a Sunday), so the first day depends on when your clerk's office opens. Registration through the BMV closes Oct 27 (carried over).

mi.name: Michigan

early.text: Early in-person voting runs at least 9 days, Sat, Oct 24 through Sun, Nov 1; some communities offer more days (up to 29 total). You can also vote absentee in person at your clerk's office, which has been open since Sep 24.

mail.text: Every registered voter can vote absentee, no reason needed. Apply online or by mail by 5 p.m. Fri, Oct 30, or in person at your clerk's office by 4 p.m. Mon, Nov 2, though the state urges applying at least 15 days ahead (that date has passed, so returning by drop box or in person is safer). Your local clerk must receive your ballot by 8 p.m. on Nov 3; postmarks do not count.

registration.sameDayText: You can register in person at your city or township clerk's office (or a satellite clerk office) through Election Day until 8 p.m., with proof of where you live, and then vote there with an absentee ballot. You can also register at an early voting site during the early voting period.
registration.text: The deadline to register online or by mail was Oct 19, but you can still register and vote by going to your clerk's office with proof of residency, including on Election Day until 8 p.m.

mi.note: Confirmed today on michigan.gov/sos: polls 7 a.m.-8 p.m. local time; mandatory early voting is at least 9 consecutive days ending the Sunday before the election (so Oct 24 to Nov 1 is the guaranteed statewide window; the exact start/end for your city is set locally); absentee online deadline 5 p.m. the Friday before (Oct 30); ballots must be received by 8 p.m. Election Day; registering within 14 days of an election, and on Election Day, is in person at a clerk's office with proof of residency; early voting sites accept same-day registration. The Nov 2 4 p.m. in-person application time and Sep 24 start are carried over. Part of Michigan's Upper Peninsula is on Central time.

mn.name: Minnesota
mn.pollHours: 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. (a few very small towns may open later, no later than 10 a.m.)

early.text: Early voting at your local election office runs Sep 18 through Mon, Nov 2. Extended hours include until 7 p.m. Tue, Oct 27, and 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. on Sat, Oct 31 and Sun, Nov 1; offices close at 5 p.m. on Nov 2.

mail.text: Any eligible voter can vote absentee, with no reason needed, and a postmark does not count: your ballot must be received by Election Day, Nov 3. If you drop it off yourself, get it to the office that sent it by 5 p.m. on Nov 3. The state suggests dropping your ballot off instead of mailing it within a week of Election Day.

registration.sameDayText: You can register at your polling place on Nov 3 (or at your local election office during early voting) by showing an accepted proof of where you live.
registration.text: The advance deadline to register was Oct 13, but you can still register on Election Day at your polling place with proof of residence.

mn.note: The Minnesota Secretary of State site put up a bot-check (Radware CAPTCHA) partway through today, so some pages could not be opened directly. Read directly today: the 'Return your ballot' page (received by Election Day, postmark does not count, drop-off by 5 p.m., mail-ballot cities until 8 p.m.). Read through the page-summary tool: the Secretary of State's 'Voting begins September 18' news release (early voting Sep 18-Nov 2, extended hours, Election Day registration available, polls until 8 p.m., pollfinder at mnvotes.gov/pollfinder) and Minnesota Statutes 204C.05 (7 a.m.-8 p.m.) and 203B.02 ('any eligible voter may vote by absentee ballot'). The advance registration deadline Oct 13 comes from the 2026 voter registration reference guide PDF and a search snippet. NOT confirmed: (1) a hard deadline to request a mail ballot (only a recommended Oct 20 date, from the Oct 19 file); (2) the news release summary says mailed absentee and mail ballots must be received by '8 p.m.' while the Return page says 5 p.m. for hand-delivery and only 'by Election Day' for mail, so no clock time is stated here for mail; (3) the polling-place finder URL was not opened. If you drop off an absentee ballot, do not take it to a polling place. The 'Agent delivery' process can return a ballot as late as 8 p.m. on Election Day. About 150,000 voters in mail-ballot precincts are mailed a ballot automatically (so allMail is false statewide).

mo.name: Missouri

early.text: Any voter can vote a no-excuse absentee ballot in person at the place your local election authority sets, starting Tuesday, Oct. 20. You can vote until 5 p.m. on Monday, Nov. 2. Show an acceptable photo ID.

mail.text: To vote by mail in Missouri you need one of the reasons on the state list, such as being away from your area on Election Day or having an illness or disability. The last day to request a mail ballot was Oct. 21 at 5 p.m. A mail ballot must reach your local election authority by the time polls close at 7 p.m. on Nov. 3.

registration.text: The deadline to register to vote in this election was Oct. 7, 2026. Missouri does not list same-day registration.

mo.note: The state's "How to Vote" page says the no-excuse in-person window starts the second Tuesday before the election (Oct. 20, my calculation) and ends the day before; it also says in-person absentee voting runs until 5 p.m. the night before. Another state FAQ says "two weeks prior." Hours and places vary by local election authority, so check yours. The mail-in return deadline comes from the state's FAQ (close of polls on Election Day); the how-to page still mentions a notary requirement for some mail ballots, so voters should ask their local office. I did not find an official statement on same-day registration; the state describes a registration deadline on the 4th Wednesday before the election.

ms.name: Mississippi

early.text: Mississippi has no open early voting. If you qualify (for example, age 65 or older, a disability, working during polling hours, or being away from home on Election Day), you can vote in person at your circuit clerk's office Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The last day is Saturday, Oct. 31, from 8 a.m. to noon.

mail.text: Mississippi mail ballots are only for certain voters, such as people 65 or older, people with a disability, or people living outside their county. The ballot must be postmarked by Nov. 3 and reach the circuit clerk's office within 5 business days (by 5 p.m. on Nov. 10). The state also tells voters to get ballots in as early as they can.

registration.text: The deadline to register to vote in this election was Oct. 5, 2026 (in person, or mailed with a postmark by that day). Mississippi does not offer same-day registration.

ms.note: Mississippi has no open early voting; both in-person absentee and mail absentee need a qualifying reason. The mail ballot rule (postmarked by Election Day, arrives within 5 business days) is the state's current rule on its Oct. 2026 notices and its 9/8/2026 calendar, but late-arriving mail ballots have been challenged in court and I could not confirm from an official source that nothing has changed, so voters should not count on the grace period. The first day of in-person absentee voting is listed as Sept. 21 on the state calendar and as Sept. 19 on the Y'all Vote page; Sept. 21 (a Monday) is used. Voters need a photo ID to vote in person.

mt.name: Montana
mt.pollHours: 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. local time (very small polling places may open later but close at 8 p.m.)

early.kind: mail ballot in person at your election office
early.text: Montana absentee ballots go out starting Oct. 9. You can fill out the request at your county election office and pick up your ballot there, then vote and return it at the office. The last day to request an absentee ballot is noon on Monday, Nov. 2. Call your county office for its hours.

mail.text: Any registered voter can vote absentee in Montana. Your ballot must be in your county election office or at your polling place by 8 p.m. on Nov. 3. A postmark does not count. The state says to mail it a week early, so with 8 days left it is safest to drop it off at your county election office now. Sign the return envelope yourself.

registration.sameDayText: After Oct. 5, you can still register or update your registration at your county election office through Election Day. You must pick up and cast your ballot in person at the election office. Ask your county office what to bring and the final cutoff time on Nov. 3.
registration.text: Regular registration closed Oct. 5, 2026. From Oct. 6 on, "late registration" is open at your county election office, where you register and get your ballot in person.

mt.note: Late registration is confusing. The state's voter site says registration is open through Election Day and ends at 8 p.m., but one line on the same page also says "through noon on Election Day," so go early and confirm the time with your county office. Another state page says a court order blocked SB 490, a law that would have opened all counties on Saturday, Oct. 31 and changed registration timing. The state calendar still lists election offices open Oct. 31, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. I could not open the state's PDF calendar, and I did not confirm what ID or proof of address late registration needs.

nc.name: North Carolina

early.text: Early voting runs Oct. 15 to Oct. 31 and ends at 3 p.m. on the last day. You can use any early voting site in your county. Sites and hours differ by county, so check your county list.

mail.text: Your mailed ballot must reach your county board of elections by 7:30 p.m. on Election Day, Nov. 3. You can also hand it in at your county board of elections office, or at any early voting site in your county during early voting.

registration.sameDayText: You can register and vote at the same time at an early voting site in your county from Oct. 15 to Oct. 31. Bring proof of where you live, such as a driver's license, paycheck, utility bill, or bank statement with your name and current address. This is not offered on Election Day.
registration.text: The regular registration deadline was 5 p.m. on Oct. 9, 2026. After that you can only register during early voting.

nc.note: The deadline to request a mail ballot was 5 p.m. on Oct. 20, so new requests are closed. If you already have a mail ballot, it cannot be handed in at a polling place on Election Day. Take it to your county board office instead, or to an early voting site before Oct. 31. On Election Day you must vote at your assigned polling place. A photo ID is required to vote in person.

nd.name: North Dakota
nd.pollHours: Set by each county. Polls open between 7 a.m. and 9 a.m. and close between 7 p.m. and 9 p.m., local time.

early.text: Only some counties offer early voting, and each sets its own dates and hours. In August the state listed Burleigh, Cass, Grand Forks, Morton, Stark, Stutsman, and Ward. Check the state's My Voting Information page for your county's dates.

mail.text: Your absentee ballot must reach your county auditor by the time polls close on Nov. 3. A postmark does not count. You can mail it (you pay for the stamp), put it in a county drop box, or hand it to the county auditor. It will not be accepted at a polling place.

registration.text: North Dakota has no voter registration. If you are 18 or older, a U.S. citizen, and have lived in your precinct for 30 days, you can just show up with a valid ID.

nd.note: Poll hours depend on the county, and western North Dakota is on Mountain time. A valid ID is required for every way of voting. A state search listing gives Nov. 2 as the absentee application deadline, but mail takes days, so that is too late for mail in practice. If you have an absentee ballot you have not returned, you can still vote at your polling place. If you already returned it, you cannot vote again. The early voting county list comes from an August state document, so confirm yours on the state portal. The 2026 mail-ballot rule 'no excuse needed' comes from that same state document.

ne.name: Nebraska
ne.pollHours: 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Central time; 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Mountain time

early.text: Early in-person voting at your county clerk or election commissioner office started Mon, Oct 5 and runs through Mon, Nov 2. Hours depend on the office.

mail.text: Any registered voter can vote early by mail, no reason needed, but the deadline to request a ballot was Fri, Oct 23. Your ballot must be in the hands of your county election office, a drop box, or other official location by the time polls close on Nov 3 (8 p.m. Central / 7 p.m. Mountain). Postmarks do not count.

registration.text: The deadlines have passed: Oct 16 to register online or by mail, and Oct 23 (6 p.m.) to register in person at your county election office. Nebraska has no Election Day registration, with a narrow exception for people who became U.S. citizens after the deadline.

ne.note: Confirmed today from the Secretary of State's 2026 Election Calendar PDF (read from a downloaded copy): first day for in-person early voting Oct 5, last day the day before the election (Nov 2), polls open 8 a.m. CT / 7 a.m. MT and close 8 p.m. CT / 7 p.m. MT, early ballot returned by mail must be in the county's possession by the closing hour, mail request due 6 p.m. on the 2nd Friday before (Oct 23), in-person registration to 6 p.m. Oct 23. The early-voting page says no reason has been needed since 1999. The state calendar also lists a late-registration exception for people who became naturalized citizens after the deadline. Eleven counties run elections entirely by mail (Boone, Cedar, Cherry, Clay, Dawes, Dixon, Garden, Knox, Merrick, Morrill, Stanton), so allMail is false statewide. The state says voter ID is required in statewide elections.

nh.name: New Hampshire
nh.pollHours: Varies by town: polls must open by 11 a.m. and close no earlier than 7 p.m. Most open between 6 and 8 a.m. Check your town.

early.text: New Hampshire has no early in-person voting. If you qualify to vote absentee, you can request and return your ballot in person at your town or city clerk's office until 5 p.m. Mon, Nov 2.

mail.text: You need a qualifying reason, such as being away on Election Day, a disability or illness, a religious observance, caring for someone or working during all polling hours, or a winter storm warning. Mail requests are due by noon Mon, Nov 2. Mailed ballots must be received by your town or city clerk by 5 p.m. on Nov 3 (delivered in person by you, the deadline is 5 p.m. Nov 2); postmarks do not count.

registration.sameDayText: You can register at your polling place on Election Day. You must be in line by the time polls close, and you will need ID and proof you live in the town.
registration.text: Registering in advance at your town or city clerk's office closed 6 to 13 days before the election (the exact date depends on your town, so it has passed). You can still register at your polling place on Election Day.

nh.note: Confirmed today on sos.nh.gov: absentee needs a qualifying reason; mail request due noon the day before the election; in-person request and return until 5 p.m. the day before; mailed or agent-delivered ballots received by 5 p.m. Election Day; registration up to 6-13 days before in person (varies by town) and at the polls on Election Day. Polling hours come from RSA 659:4 (open no later than 11 a.m., close no earlier than 7 p.m.) as read through a search summary of the state statute site, plus the Secretary of State's media guide; exact hours are set by each town or city and are listed in the state's voter lookup. The state site never says 'no early voting' in so many words; absentee voting is the only option before Election Day.

nj.name: New Jersey

early.text: You can vote in person at an early voting site in your county from Oct. 24 to Nov. 1. Hours are Monday to Saturday 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. and Sunday 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. No appointment needed.

mail.text: A mailed ballot must be postmarked by 8 p.m. on Election Day (Nov. 3) and reach your county Board of Elections by Nov. 9. You can also drop it in a county ballot drop box or hand it to your county Board of Elections office by 8 p.m. on Nov. 3.

registration.text: The deadline to register to vote in the November election was Oct. 13, 2026.

nj.note: The deadline to request a mail ballot by mail was Oct. 27. You can still pick one up in person from your county clerk until 3 p.m. on Nov. 2. You cannot turn in a mail ballot at your polling place or early voting site, only at the county Board of Elections office or a county drop box. A ballot with no postmark that arrives by Nov. 5 can still count, but do not count on that. If you are set up to vote by mail and want to vote early in person instead, contact your county clerk first to opt out. The state pages do not list any same-day registration, so sameDay is false from that absence. The NJ vote-by-mail page prints a few dates labeled 'November 2, 2026' that appear to be the in-person pickup cutoff for the day before Election Day.

nm.name: New Mexico

early.text: Early voting started Oct. 6 at your county clerk's office and ends Saturday, Oct. 31. More early voting sites open in many counties from Oct. 17, so check your county clerk for locations and hours.

mail.text: Your mailed ballot must reach your county clerk by 7 p.m. on Election Day, Nov. 3. A postmark does not count. You can also drop it at the county clerk's office, any early voting or Election Day voting site, or an official drop box in your county.

registration.sameDayText: You can register or update your registration and vote on the same day at your county clerk's office, an early voting site, or your polling place on Election Day. At a polling place, bring a photo ID (it can be expired). If the address on it does not match, bring a recent bill, bank statement, or paycheck showing your address.
registration.text: The regular online or mail registration deadline was Oct. 6, 2026. After that you can still register in person and vote the same day.

nm.note: The deadline to request a mail ballot was Oct. 20, so new requests are closed. The state says that if you have not mailed your ballot by Oct. 27, you should return it in person instead. Some state web pages still show an old 2021 banner date; ignore it.

nv.name: Nevada

early.text: Early voting runs Saturday, Oct. 17 through Friday, Oct. 30. Your county sets the places and hours. You can also register and vote on the same visit.

mail.text: Nevada mails a ballot to every active registered voter unless they opted out. Mail it so it is postmarked by Nov. 3 and it counts if your county gets it by Nov. 7. You can also use any official drop box in your county until polls close on Nov. 3. The state suggests mailing at least a week before Election Day.

registration.sameDayText: You can register or update your registration in person during early voting or on Election Day at a polling place. You need a valid Nevada driver's license or Nevada ID card, plus proof of where you live if your ID does not show your current address.
registration.text: Oct. 20, 2026 was the last day to register or update your registration and be mailed a ballot. After that, you can still register in person during early voting or on Election Day.

nv.note: If you registered or updated online less than 14 days before the election (after Oct. 20), you may only vote in person with your Nevada driver's license or ID. Voters whose mail ballot signature is missing or does not match have until 5 p.m. Pacific on Nov. 9 to fix it, so answer calls, texts, and mail from the county. Same-day registration requires a Nevada driver's license or ID card (a military ID or passport cannot prove identity for this), and the ballot may be provisional.

ny.name: New York

early.text: Early voting runs Oct. 24 to Nov. 1. Each county board of elections sets the daily hours. Outside New York City you can use any early voting site in your county. In New York City you are assigned one site.

mail.text: A mailed ballot must be postmarked by Nov. 3 and reach your county board of elections by Nov. 10. You can also hand it in at your county board office by 9 p.m. on Nov. 3, at an early voting site Oct. 24 to Nov. 1, or at a poll site in your county by 9 p.m. on Nov. 3.

registration.text: The deadline to register to vote in the November election was Oct. 24, 2026.

ny.note: New York calls its no-reason mail ballot an 'early mail ballot'. The deadline to ask for one by mail or online was Oct. 24. You can still request one in person at your county board of elections until Nov. 2. If you were already sent a mail ballot, you cannot use a voting machine. You would vote on an affidavit ballot instead, and it only counts if your mail ballot never arrives. A ballot put in a mailbox after the last pickup on Nov. 3 gets a Nov. 4 postmark and will not count, so use a drop-off instead. The 6 a.m. to 9 p.m. poll hours come from the state's own time-off-to-vote page. The state registration pages list no same-day registration, so sameDay is false from that absence.

oh.name: Ohio

early.text: Early voting at your county board of elections runs Oct. 6 to Nov. 1. Hours change by day, such as 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on Saturday, Oct. 31 and 1 p.m. to 5 p.m. on Sunday, Nov. 1.

mail.text: Your mailed ballot must reach your county board of elections by 7:30 p.m. on Election Day, Nov. 3. A postmark does not count. You or a close relative can also hand it in at the board office or its drop box by 7:30 p.m. on Nov. 3.

registration.text: The deadline to register to vote in the November election was Oct. 5, 2026.

oh.note: The last day for your county board to receive a mail ballot request is Oct. 27 at 8:30 p.m. Mail is too slow for that now, so request in person at your board. The state's schedule ends early voting on Sunday, Nov. 1. A valid photo ID is needed to vote in person. The state pages list no same-day registration, so sameDay is false from that absence.

ok.name: Oklahoma

early.text: You can vote early at your county election board's early voting location on Wed. Oct. 28, Thu. Oct. 29, and Fri. Oct. 30 from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., and Sat. Oct. 31 from 8 a.m. to 2 p.m. No reason is needed. You must vote in the county where you are registered.

mail.text: A mailed absentee ballot must reach your county election board by 7 p.m. on Election Day, Nov. 3. A postmark does not count. If you hand-deliver it, it must be there by the end of business on Monday, Nov. 2.

registration.text: The deadline to register to vote in the November election was Oct. 9, 2026.

ok.note: The deadline to request a mail ballot was 5 p.m. on Oct. 19, so new requests are closed. A standard mail ballot must be notarized. Oklahoma calls early voting 'in-person absentee' voting. Early voting is short, only four days. You need proof of identity to vote. The state pages list no same-day registration, so sameDay is false from that absence.

or.name: Oregon
or.pollHours: Oregon has no polling places. Drop boxes are open until 8 p.m. on Election Day, and county elections offices are open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.

early.text: Oregon votes by mail. Ballots were mailed starting Oct. 14, so you can fill yours out at home and return it any time before Election Day.

mail.text: Put your ballot in an official drop box by 8 p.m. on Nov. 3. If you mail it instead, it must be postmarked by Nov. 3 and arrive within 7 days after Election Day, by Nov. 10. The state's last recommended day to mail is Oct. 27.

registration.text: The deadline to register to vote in the November election was Oct. 13, 2026.

or.note: The state's last recommended day to mail a ballot is Oct. 27 (tomorrow), so from now on a drop box is the safe choice. A mailed ballot only counts if the post office puts a postmark on it showing it was mailed by Nov. 3. Mail dropped after the last pickup on Nov. 3 may get a Nov. 4 postmark. Ballots are not mailed to voters marked inactive; check your status in MyVote. Use the state's Ballot Drop Box Locator for drop box hours. The state pages list no same-day registration, so sameDay is false from that absence.

pa.name: Pennsylvania
pa.pollHours: 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. (anyone in line at 8 p.m. can vote)

early.kind: mail ballot in person at your election office
early.text: Pennsylvania has no traditional early voting, but you can request, fill out, and turn in a mail ballot in one visit to your county elections office or another designated site. The window for applying closes 5 p.m. Tue, Oct 27, and when it opens depends on when your county has ballots ready.

mail.text: Any registered voter can vote by mail, no reason needed. Applications must reach your county by 5 p.m. Tue, Oct 27. Your county elections office must receive the ballot by 8 p.m. on Nov 3; a postmark is not enough. You can hand your own ballot in at your county office until 8 p.m. on Election Day if you applied by the deadline.

registration.text: The deadline to register was Oct 19, so it has passed. Pennsylvania has no Election Day registration. If you are already registered, you can still vote.

pa.note: Confirmed today on pa.gov/agencies/vote: no-excuse mail-in (absentee needs a reason); application due 5 p.m. Oct 27; received by 8 p.m. Nov 3 with the state saying a postmark by 8 p.m. is not sufficient; in-person mail ballot at the county office with drop-off until 8 p.m. on Election Day; emergency absentee ballot possible after Oct 27 for an unexpected illness, disability, or last-minute absence; polls 7 a.m.-8 p.m. Early start is null because it depends on each county's ballots being ready. Voter trap: if you return a voted mail ballot you cannot vote at your polling place. Unsigned or undated outer envelopes and ballots not sealed in the inner 'Official Election Ballot' envelope are not counted.

ri.name: Rhode Island
ri.pollHours: 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. (New Shoreham on Block Island opens at 9 a.m.)

early.text: You can vote in person at your city or town hall (or another site your local board picks) from Oct. 14 to Nov. 2, during regular business hours. Bring a photo ID.

mail.text: Your mail ballot must reach the state Board of Elections by 8 p.m. on Election Day, Nov. 3. A postmark does not count. You can mail it, put it in an official drop box, or hand it to the Board of Elections in Cranston.

registration.text: The deadline to register to vote in the November election was Oct. 4, 2026. Same-day registration in Rhode Island is only for presidential elections, so it is not offered this year.

ri.note: The normal mail ballot request deadline was 4 p.m. on Oct. 13. From Oct. 14 to Nov. 2 you can still get an emergency mail ballot by going to your local board of canvassers. The state's date chart is a spreadsheet on the state site that still mixes in some 2024 rows. The 2026 rows used here match the state's registration, early voting, and mail ballot pages. The state advises allowing 7 mailing days. You must show a photo ID to vote in person, or you vote an emergency mail ballot.

sc.name: South Carolina

early.text: Early voting runs Monday, Oct. 19 to Saturday, Oct. 31, from 8:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. Centers are closed on Sunday, Oct. 25. No reason is needed. Early voting centers can be different from your Election Day polling place.

mail.text: You need a qualifying reason to vote by mail, such as being 65 or older, having a disability, or being away. Your ballot must reach your county voter registration office by 7 p.m. on Nov. 3. A postmark does not count. You can also hand it in at your county office or an early voting center, with a photo ID.

registration.text: The deadline to register to vote in the November election was Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026.

sc.note: The deadline to return a mail ballot application was 5 p.m. on Oct. 23, so new mail ballot requests are closed. If you do not have a mail ballot, vote early (through Oct. 31) or on Election Day. A mail ballot must be signed with a witness who is 18 or older; a notary is not needed. A photo ID is needed to vote in person and to hand in a ballot. Anyone in line at 7 p.m. may still vote. The state pages list no same-day registration, so sameDay is false from that absence.

sd.name: South Dakota
sd.pollHours: 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. local time (South Dakota has two time zones, Central and Mountain)

early.text: You can vote in person at your county auditor's office with a photo ID. This started September 18 and runs until at least 5 p.m. on Monday, November 2.

mail.text: Your mail ballot must reach your county election office on Election Day in time to be taken to your voting precinct before the polls close at 7 p.m. local time. A postmark does not count, so with so little time left it is safer to hand-deliver it to your county auditor's office.

registration.text: The registration deadline was Monday, October 19 at 5 p.m. local time, which is 15 days before Election Day. The official sources do not list same-day registration.

sd.note: The state absentee page says you 'may be eligible' if you cannot go to your polling place, but it does not clearly say whether you need a reason, so mail.noExcuse is null. The same page says anyone registered can vote in person at the auditor's office once absentee voting starts. The request deadline for a mailed ballot is 5 p.m. on Nov 2 (official calendar), but a ballot requested this late will almost certainly not make it back in time, so voters should go in person. A voter confined by sickness or disability can send an authorized messenger until 3 p.m. on Election Day. Ballots delivered after the polls close are not counted.

tn.name: Tennessee
tn.pollHours: Opening time depends on the county. All polls close at 7 p.m. Central or 8 p.m. Eastern. Anyone in line at closing can still vote.

early.text: Early voting runs Wednesday, October 14 through Thursday, October 29. That means this week is your last chance to vote early. Hours and places depend on your county.

mail.text: Tennessee only lets people vote by mail for certain reasons, such as being 60 or older, being sick or disabled, or being out of the county the whole voting period. The ballot must reach your county election office by the time polls close on Election Day. You must return it by mail or delivery service. Handing it in at an early voting site or polling place is not allowed. The request deadline was October 24.

registration.text: The registration deadline was Monday, October 5, 2026. Tennessee does not offer same-day registration.

tn.note: You need a photo ID to vote in person; student IDs and out-of-state licenses are not accepted. The poll-hours wording comes from the state's August 2026 election release; the state calendar does not list November poll hours, so check your county's hours in the GoVoteTN app. The state calendar does not mention same-day registration anywhere; the registration deadline is the cutoff.

tx.name: Texas
tx.pollHours: 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. at all polling places statewide (local time; El Paso area is on Mountain Time)

early.text: Early voting is Monday, October 19 through Friday, October 30. You can vote at any early voting site in your county. Hours differ by site.

mail.text: Texas only lets some people vote by mail: age 65 or older, sick or disabled, out of the county the whole voting period, expecting a baby within three weeks, or in jail. A ballot with no postmark must arrive by 7 p.m. on Election Day. A ballot postmarked by 7 p.m. on Election Day can arrive until 5 p.m. on Wednesday, November 4. You can also hand-deliver it to your county early voting clerk's office on Election Day.

registration.text: The registration deadline was Monday, October 5, 2026. Texas does not offer same-day registration.

tx.note: Postmarks can be late: the state warns USPS sometimes postmarks mail a day after you drop it off. Ask for a free hand postmark at a post office counter. The application deadline for a mail ballot was October 23, so only people who already have a ballot can use mail now. On Election Day, some counties let you vote at any site (vote centers) and others make you use your own precinct, so check your county. Bring one of the seven accepted photo IDs.

ut.name: Utah

early.text: In-person early voting is October 20 through October 30. Every county offers it, but days, hours and places differ, so check with your county clerk.

mail.text: Active registered voters are mailed a ballot automatically. Your county clerk must have your ballot by 8 p.m. on Election Day, November 3. A postmark does not count. You can also use an official drop box until 8 p.m. on Election Day.

registration.sameDayText: You can register in person during early voting or on Election Day at a vote center. Bring two forms of valid ID, including proof of where you live.
registration.text: Online and mail registration closed Friday, October 23 at 5 p.m. You can still register in person during early voting or on Election Day.

ut.note: Big trap: Utah no longer counts postmarks. A ballot that is mailed on or before Election Day but arrives later is not counted. Mail by now is risky; use a drop box or take it to your clerk. Drop boxes close at 8 p.m. The last day to request a replacement mail ballot was October 27 at 5 p.m. The early voting dates (Oct 20 to Oct 30) come from the state voter pamphlet and calendar; counties set their own hours.

va.name: Virginia
va.pollHours: 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. Anyone in line at 7 p.m. can still vote.

early.text: Anyone registered can vote early in person at their local registrar's office or an early voting site. It ends at 5 p.m. on Saturday, October 31. Hours and places differ by locality, so call your registrar.

mail.text: Anyone can vote by mail without giving a reason. A mailed ballot must be postmarked by Election Day and arrive at your registrar's office by noon on Friday, November 6. You can also hand it in at the registrar's office, a drop-off site during early voting, or your polling place on Election Day (by 7 p.m.). The request deadline was October 23.

registration.sameDayText: After October 23 you can still register in person at your registrar's office or an early voting site, or at your polling place on Election Day. You vote a provisional ballot, which is counted after election officials check that you are eligible.
registration.text: The regular registration deadline was Friday, October 23. After that you can still register and vote with a provisional ballot.

va.note: A mailed ballot with no postmark may not be counted, so take it inside a post office and ask for a postmark, or hand-deliver it. People who register after the Oct 23 deadline vote on a provisional ballot, which takes extra steps to count. A first-time mail voter who registered by mail may need to include a copy of an ID with the ballot. The state's same-day registration page still mentions an October 24 date from an older election; the current 2026 deadline on the Upcoming Elections page is October 23.

vt.name: Vermont
vt.pollHours: Each town opens its polls between 5 a.m. and 10 a.m. All polls close at 7 p.m.

early.text: You can vote early in person at your town or city clerk's office during its business hours. Early voting starts 45 days before the election or as soon as ballots are ready in your town.

mail.text: Active voters were mailed a ballot automatically. To be safe, your town clerk should have it before the clerk's office closes on Monday, November 2. You can also bring your ballot to your polling place before 7 p.m. on Election Day or drop it in your town's drop box.

registration.sameDayText: You can register up to and including Election Day. Register at your town or city clerk's office during business hours before Election Day, or at your polling place on Election Day. First-time voters who register online or by mail must include a copy of an ID such as a driver's license, utility bill or bank statement.
registration.text: Vermont has no registration deadline. You can register any day through Election Day.

vt.note: The state page lists the mail-return deadline as the clerk's office closing time the day before the election, not the end of Election Day. It does not give a date for how late a mailed ballot can arrive, so mail it right away or hand it in. If you lost your ballot or did not get it, you can still vote at the polls by signing an Affidavit of No Ballot Cast. The 'start' date for early voting (Sept 19) is 45 days before Nov 3; the state says towns may start as soon as ballots are ready.

wa.name: Washington
wa.pollHours: There are no neighborhood polling places. Official drop boxes and voting centers close at 8 p.m. on Election Day. Voting center hours differ by county.

early.text: Voting centers in each county are open from 18 days before Election Day (October 16) until 8 p.m. on Election Day. You can register, get a replacement ballot, or vote there. Hours differ by county.

mail.text: Every registered voter was mailed a ballot by October 16. Put it in an official drop box by 8 p.m. on Election Day, or mail it with a postmark dated no later than November 3. Mailed ballots must arrive by the close of business on the day before your county certifies results (Nov 23 for counties that certify Nov 24).

registration.sameDayText: You can register or update your registration in person at your county elections office or voting center until 8 p.m. on Election Day.
registration.text: The online and mail registration deadline is today, Monday, October 26. After that, register in person at a voting center until 8 p.m. on Election Day.

wa.note: The state says USPS recommends mailing your ballot at least a week before Election Day (October 27), and postmarks are not always applied the same day, so use a drop box now. Meter stamps or dated postage do not count as a postmark. The last-arrival date of Nov 23 comes from state rule WAC 434-250-120 ('day before certification') together with the state fact sheet's Nov 24 certification date; individual counties may certify on different days. Washington has no early-voting window in the usual sense: voting centers are the in-person option.

wi.name: Wisconsin
wi.pollHours: 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Anyone in line by 8 p.m. can vote.

early.text: In-person absentee voting at your municipal clerk's office or other site runs from October 20 at the earliest to Sunday, November 1 at the latest. Each town sets its own days and hours, and some stop earlier, so call your clerk.

mail.text: Any registered voter can vote by mail with no reason. Your ballot must be in the hands of election officials by 8 p.m. on Election Day. A postmark does not count. The online or mail request deadline is 5 p.m. on Thursday, October 29. You can drop it off at your clerk's office, polling place, or drop box if your town has one.

registration.sameDayText: You can register at your polling place on Election Day. Bring proof of where you live (for example a lease or utility bill), and bring your photo ID because you need it to get a ballot. You can also register in person at your clerk's office until the Friday before the election (Oct 30) at 5 p.m. or closing.
registration.text: The online and mail registration deadline was Wednesday, October 14. You can still register in person.

wi.note: You cannot ask for a ballot in person and take it home: in-person absentee ballots are voted in the clerk's office. Mailing a ballot now is risky because postmarks do not count; hand-deliver it. The 8 p.m. closing time comes from the state calendar and an August 2026 state reminder. You need a photo ID to vote. If you moved within Wisconsin in the last 28 days, you may have to vote from your old address.

wv.name: West Virginia

early.text: Early voting is Wednesday, October 21 through Saturday, October 31 at your county courthouse, an annex or another site your county picks. Hours vary by county, with Saturday hours usually 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.

mail.text: You need an allowed reason to vote by mail, such as being sick, disabled, or away from your county for the whole voting period. Your application must reach your county clerk by October 28. Your ballot must be postmarked by Election Day and reach the clerk before the county vote count starts (November 9 on the state calendar). If you hand-deliver it, it must be at the clerk's office by Monday, November 2.

registration.text: The registration deadline was Tuesday, October 13, 2026. West Virginia does not offer same-day registration for most voters.

wv.note: A mailed absentee ballot with no postmark can still count if it arrives by Wednesday, November 4. Because USPS may not postmark right away, mail it early or hand-deliver it. The state calendar lists November 9 as when postmarked ballots are accepted, tied to the start of the county canvass (vote count review); treat it as the outside limit and do not wait. Emergency absentee ballots are available October 27 to noon on November 3 for people who become confined by illness or injury or are in the hospital. Only a few special groups can register late. You need a photo ID to vote in person.

wy.name: Wyoming

early.text: You can vote in person at your county clerk's office from October 6 through Monday, November 2. This is called absentee voting, but you can do it in person.

mail.text: Any registered voter can ask for an absentee ballot, with no reason needed, but not on Election Day itself. Your county clerk must have your ballot by 7 p.m. on Election Day. Late ballots are not counted. Mail can take up to seven days, so hand-delivering it to the clerk is safer now.

registration.sameDayText: You can register and vote at your polling place on Election Day. You can also register in person at the county clerk's office and vote absentee from October 20 to November 2. Bring proof of citizenship and proof of Wyoming residency.
registration.text: Normal registration closed Monday, October 19. You can still register at your county clerk's office or at your polling place on Election Day.

wy.note: The state's 2026 voter guide says mail or in-person registration closes 'not less than 14 days' before the election, while the state's Key Election Dates and calendar list October 19 (15 days). Either way, same-day registration at the polls is available. You must show an accepted photo ID to vote in person. A voter who moved counties must re-register in the new county.

calendar.title: Medicare Open Enrollment
calendar.text: If you have Medicare, this is the window to join, drop, or switch Medicare Advantage and drug (Part D) plans for 2027. Compare your current plan to the 2027 options before it ends.
calendar.note: Window is already underway on 2026-10-26. Coverage changes start January 1, 2027. The plan must receive your request by December 7.

calendar.title: HealthCare.gov sign-up opens for 2027
calendar.text: You can apply for, renew, or change a 2027 health plan on HealthCare.gov from November 1 through January 15. Sign up by December 15 if you want coverage to start January 1.
calendar.note: HealthCare.gov (federal marketplace) dates are Nov 1, 2026 to Jan 15, 2027. A 2025 CMS rule would have ended the federal window Dec 15 starting with plan year 2027, but CMS's Aug 4, 2026 court-litigation statement says the federal window will begin Nov 1, 2026 and end Jan 15, 2027 (https://www.cms.gov/files/document/statement-re-city-columbus-080426.pdf). State-run marketplaces set their own dates and can differ, so check your state's site.

calendar.title: Clocks fall back one hour
calendar.text: Daylight saving time ends at 2 a.m. local time on Sunday, so clocks go back to 1 a.m. and you get an extra hour. Hawaii and most of Arizona do not change their clocks.
calendar.note: NIST also lists American Samoa, Guam, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands as not observing DST. The Navajo Nation inside Arizona does change its clocks.

calendar.title: Election Day
calendar.text: This is the general election for all 435 U.S. House seats, 35 U.S. Senate seats, 36 governorships and many state and local races. Check your registration and polling place before you go, and bring any ID your state requires.
calendar.note: Rules for ID, early voting, mail ballots and registration deadlines are set by each state, and poll hours vary. vote.gov and usa.gov/election-day point people to their state.

calendar.title: Veterans Day
calendar.text: Federal offices are closed on this federal holiday, and the post office usually does not deliver regular mail. Many banks and some state or local offices close too, so check before you head out.
calendar.note: OPM list confirms the date (Wednesday). The mail statement is the usual USPS practice for federal holidays; no 2026 Veterans Day USPS notice was found, so confirm on usps.com.

calendar.title: Thanksgiving Day
calendar.text: Federal offices are closed and there is normally no regular mail delivery. Banks and many government offices are closed too.
calendar.note: Date confirmed by OPM. Mail closure is the usual USPS practice; check usps.com.

calendar.title: Last day to change Medicare plans
calendar.text: This is the last day of Medicare Open Enrollment. If you want a different Medicare Advantage or drug plan for 2027, your request has to be in by today.

calendar.title: Deadline for Jan. 1 health coverage
calendar.text: On HealthCare.gov, pick or change a plan by this date for coverage to start January 1, 2027, and pay your first premium. Sign up later and coverage starts February 1.
calendar.note: Applies to the federal marketplace (HealthCare.gov). State-run marketplaces may have a different cutoff for January 1 coverage.

calendar.title: Christmas Day
calendar.text: Federal offices are closed and there is normally no regular mail delivery. If a bill or benefit is due around this day, plan for it to arrive a day early or late.
calendar.note: Date confirmed by OPM, which lists no extra December 24 or 26 holiday for 2026. Mail closure is the usual USPS practice; check usps.com.

calendar.title: SSI raise shows up in payments
calendar.text: About 7.3 million people on SSI get their January payment on December 31, with the 3.6 percent cost-of-living raise included. Nothing to sign up for; it is automatic.
calendar.note: SSA announced the 2027 COLA on Oct 14, 2026. January 1 is a holiday, so SSI's January payment is made at the end of December.

calendar.title: Medicaid work rules begin by Jan. 1
calendar.text: States must start requiring many adults ages 19 to 64 in the Medicaid expansion group to show 80 hours a month of work, volunteering, school or a work program. Many people are exempt, such as parents of young children and people who are medically frail. If you are on Medicaid, watch for a letter from your state and ask the state agency whether this applies to you.
calendar.note: CMS says states must implement 'no later than January 1, 2027' and may start earlier. Details and exemptions vary by state; this is an interim final rule (published June 3, 2026) and CMS says it may change.

calendar.title: Medicare Advantage switch window
calendar.text: If you're in a Medicare Advantage plan, you can switch to a different one or go back to Original Medicare, once, before March 31.

calendar.title: New Year's Day
calendar.text: Federal offices are closed and there is normally no regular mail delivery. Banks are usually closed too.
calendar.note: Friday. Mail closure is the usual USPS practice; check usps.com.

calendar.title: Social Security raises 3.6 percent
calendar.text: Nearly 72 million people on Social Security will see a 3.6 percent bigger payment starting in January 2027. You do not have to apply; look for a letter from Social Security in December.
calendar.note: SSA says the raise begins in January 2027 benefits. The exact deposit day depends on each person's usual payment schedule. SSA also set the 2027 maximum taxable earnings at $192,300.

calendar.title: Last day to sign up on HealthCare.gov
calendar.text: Open Enrollment on HealthCare.gov ends today. After this you can only get a marketplace plan if you qualify for a Special Enrollment Period, such as losing other coverage.
calendar.note: Federal marketplace only. Sign-ups from Dec 16 through Jan 15 start coverage Feb 1. State-run marketplaces can end on other dates.

calendar.title: Last 2026 estimated tax payment due
calendar.text: If you make quarterly estimated tax payments (for example, self-employed or gig income), the fourth 2026 payment is due this day. If you file your full 2026 return and pay by January 31, 2027, you can skip it.
calendar.note: From IRS Publication 505 (2026), which gives January 15, 2027 for the final payment and the January 31 file-and-pay exception. January 15, 2027 is a Friday.
