ballot.note: Senate: senate.gov lists exactly 33 Class II states (terms end Jan 3, 2027), which are the 33 regular races. Florida and Ohio are the two specials (35 total): senate.gov lists Ashley Moody (FL) and Jon Husted (OH) in Class III (terms end Jan 3, 2029), meaning they hold seats vacated mid-term, and Ohio county election-board notices label the race 'unexpired term ending 1-3-2029'. Florida's own Division of Elections candidate list simply calls the race 'United States Senator' with no 'special' label, so FL's special status rests on the Class III term-end date (medium-high confidence). Governor: NGA counts 39 gubernatorial elections in 2026, which is the 36 states listed plus 3 territories (Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, U.S. Virgin Islands); the 36 states match the expected count. All 435 U.S. House seats are on the ballot and D.C. elects a non-voting delegate (standard fact, not separately re-fetched from a primary page). Runoffs after Nov 3 in some states were not researched.

races.note: No debate. Same forum, same questions · 5 questions

al.title: Local elections in four cities
al.what: Voters in Montgomery, Mountain Brook, Scottsboro and Talladega have local elections or referendums (local ballot questions) on this day.
al.note: The Secretary of State lists only these four cities for this date. Other Alabama towns may have different dates. The 2028 primary date is computed from the "first Tuesday in March" rule in Code of Alabama 17-13-3 (the source shown is the legislature bill that moved the primary to that day); the Secretary of State has not posted a 2028 calendar yet.

ak.title: Anchorage city election
ak.what: Voters in the Municipality of Anchorage choose city officials (such as Assembly and school board seats) and vote on local questions.
ak.note: Computed from the state calendar, which lists the 2026 Anchorage election on the first Tuesday in April (April 7, 2026). The 2027 date and the 30-days-before registration deadline have not been posted yet.

ak.title: Borough, city and rural school board elections
ak.what: Many Alaska boroughs and cities hold their regular local elections on this day, and the state also runs elections for rural school boards (called REAAs) in areas outside organized boroughs.
ak.note: Computed from the state calendar, which lists the 2026 regular municipal elections and rural school board election on the first Tuesday in October (October 6, 2026). Not every town uses this date; Anchorage uses April.

az.title: March local election day
az.what: Cities, towns, school districts and other local governments may hold elections on local ballot questions such as bonds or budget overrides. Not every community has one.
az.note: Listed on the Secretary of State 2025-2026 election calendar as the "March Next Odd Year Election" under A.R.S. 16-204, with the registration deadline shown there.

az.title: May local election day
az.what: Local governments may hold elections on local ballot questions such as bonds or budget overrides. Not every community has one.
az.note: Date listed on the Secretary of State calendar. The registration deadline is computed as 29 days before, the same rule the state shows for the March date.

az.title: November local election day
az.what: Cities, towns, counties, school districts and other local governments may put local ballot questions (such as tax or bond measures) to voters. People are not elected on this date in odd years.
az.note: Computed from A.R.S. 16-204: first Tuesday after the first Monday in November. Registration deadline computed as 29 days before the election.

ar.title: General runoff (county and city races)
ar.what: If no candidate wins a majority in some county or city races on November 3, the top candidates face off in a runoff.
ar.note: The state calendar lists the registration deadline as Sunday, November 1 but says the actual deadline moves to Monday, November 2, 2026.

ar.title: School elections and local ballot questions in 2027
ar.what: Some Arkansas school districts and local governments may hold school board elections or vote on local questions in 2027, but the date depends on the district.
ar.note: Arkansas 2025 laws (Acts 405 and 503) moved most school board elections to the even-year primary or November general election. The bill text we could read still mentions odd-year dates, but we could not confirm the exact 2027 days, so none is given. Ask your county clerk or school district.

ca.title: March local election day
ca.what: Cities, school districts and other local agencies may hold elections on this day, including special elections to fill vacancies. Not every community has one.
ca.note: Computed from California Elections Code 1000(b): first Tuesday after the first Monday in March of odd-numbered years. Whether any election happens depends on your local agency or any special election called by the state.

ca.title: November local election day
ca.what: Many city councils, school boards and special districts hold their regular elections, and local ballot measures appear, on this day.
ca.note: Computed from California Elections Code 1000(e): first Tuesday after the first Monday in November. Whether you have a ballot depends on your city, school district or special district.

co.title: Coordinated election
co.what: Local governments such as school boards, special districts and some cities hold elections and ballot questions on this day, and any statewide ballot questions go on it too. All voting is by mail ballot.
co.note: Colorado has same-day voter registration, so people can register through Election Day. The state calendar also lists 2027 deadlines for this election.

ct.title: Municipal election
ct.what: Every Connecticut town and city elects local officials such as mayor or first selectman, council and school board members, and may vote on local questions.
ct.note: Computed from Connecticut General Statutes 9-164: Tuesday after the first Monday of November in odd-numbered years. A town can instead hold it on the first Monday in May (May 3, 2027) if its council votes by a three-fourths majority, so check your town clerk.

de.title: School board elections
de.what: Voters in each Delaware school district elect school board members and may vote on school funding questions.
de.note: Computed from Delaware Code Title 14, section 1072(c): school board elections are held annually on the second Tuesday of May. Voters do not need to be registered for the general election to vote in school board elections.

de.title: Town and city elections
de.what: Delaware towns and cities set their own election dates for mayor and council, so each community differs.
de.note: The Department of Elections publishes a separate "Delaware Municipal Elections Calendar" each year; the 2027 one is not posted yet.

dc.title: Special elections if a seat opens
dc.what: If a D.C. Council, school board or neighborhood commission seat becomes vacant, the Board of Elections schedules a special election.
dc.note: No special election dated after November 3, 2026 was found on official D.C. pages.

fl.title: Local and special elections
fl.what: Florida cities and special districts hold their own elections (many in spring) and the state can call special elections when a legislative or congressional seat opens.
fl.note: The state listed no special election dated after November 3, 2026 as of July 2026. The state also keeps a Local Elections Database where counties report local dates.

ga.title: General election runoff
ga.what: If no candidate gets more than half the votes in a race on November 3, the top two face off in a runoff.
ga.note: November 2, 2026 is the last day to register for the runoff, as listed on georgia.gov.

ga.title: Special election day for local questions
ga.what: Counties, cities and school districts may hold special elections on local ballot questions this day.
ga.note: Computed from Georgia law (O.C.G.A. 21-2-540) as quoted in the legislature's 2026 bill text: in odd years special elections for questions are held on the third Tuesday in March or the Tuesday after the first Monday in November. A 2026 bill (SB 514) would also add June and September dates; we did not confirm whether it became law. Whether any election is held depends on local calls.

ga.title: Municipal and special election day
ga.what: Georgia cities elect mayors and council members in odd years, and local ballot questions may be voted on this day.
ga.note: Computed: Tuesday after the first Monday in November of odd-numbered years, the date Georgia law uses for municipal general elections and special elections. Not every city has an election; check with your city or county.

id.title: May election day
id.what: Cities, school districts and other local governments may hold elections on local questions such as school levies and bonds. Not every community has one.
id.note: Computed from Idaho Code 34-106: elections may be held on the third Tuesday in May. Idaho allows same-day voter registration, so there is no separate deadline.

id.title: November election day
id.what: Idaho cities elect mayors and city council members in odd years, and local questions can be on the ballot (including city initiatives and referendums).
id.note: Computed from Idaho Code 34-106: Tuesday following the first Monday in November.

il.title: Consolidated primary election
il.what: Voters nominate candidates for city, village, township, school board and other local offices in places that hold primary-style elections.
il.note: Computed from 10 ILCS 5/2A-1.1(b): last Tuesday in February of odd-numbered years. Many places have no primary because too few people file for the offices.

il.title: Consolidated election
il.what: Voters elect mayors, councils, school boards, township and other local officials and may vote on local questions.
il.note: Computed from 10 ILCS 5/2A-1.1(b): first Tuesday in April of odd-numbered years.

in.title: Municipal primary election
in.what: Voters in cities and larger towns pick party nominees for mayor, council and other city or town offices.
in.note: The state calendar lists May 4, 2027 as Municipal Primary Election Day. The registration deadline is computed as 29 days before the election (Indiana's usual rule) and has not been separately posted yet.

in.title: Municipal election
in.what: Voters elect mayors, city and town councils, clerks and other local officials.
in.note: The state calendar lists November 2, 2027 as Municipal Election Day. The registration deadline is computed as 29 days before the election.

ia.title: Public measure election day
ia.what: Counties, cities and school districts may hold elections on local ballot questions (public measures) on this day.
ia.note: Computed from Iowa Code 39.2 as described by the Secretary of State: first Tuesday in March. Only happens if a local government calls one.

ia.title: Public measure election day
ia.what: Counties, cities and school districts may hold elections on local ballot questions (public measures) on this day.
ia.note: Computed from Iowa Code 39.2 as described by the Secretary of State: second Tuesday in September. Only happens if a local government calls one.

ia.title: City primary
ia.what: In cities that use primaries, voters narrow the list of candidates for mayor and city council.
ia.note: The state lists this date as the voter pre-registration deadline; Iowa also allows same-day registration at the polls.

ia.title: Regular city and school election
ia.what: Voters elect city officials (mayors, councils) and school board members and may vote on public measures.
ia.note: The state lists this date as the voter pre-registration deadline; Iowa also allows same-day registration at the polls.

ia.title: City runoff
ia.what: If no candidate wins enough votes in some city races on November 2, the top candidates face a runoff.
ia.note: The state lists this date as the voter pre-registration deadline.

ks.title: City and school primary
ks.what: Where more candidates file than seats, voters narrow the field for city and school board offices.
ks.note: Computed from K.S.A. 25-2107: a primary may be held the first Tuesday in August of odd years, if needed. Many places have no primary.

ks.title: City and school election
ks.what: Voters elect city council members, mayors and school board members and may vote on local questions.
ks.note: Computed from K.S.A. 25-2107: Tuesday following the first Monday in November of odd and even years.

ky.title: Primary election
ky.what: Voters pick each party's candidates for governor and the other statewide offices (such as attorney general and secretary of state).
ky.note: Date is the first Tuesday after the third Monday in May (KRS 118.025) and is printed on the State Board of Elections 2027 calendar.

ky.title: General election
ky.what: Voters choose the governor and other statewide offices, such as lieutenant governor, attorney general and secretary of state.

la.title: Runoff and general election (December)
la.what: Runoff for races where nobody won a majority on Nov 3, including U.S. House seats and local offices, plus a special primary for one Baton Rouge-area state Senate seat.
la.note: Only voters in places with a race that needs a second round can vote. Dates are subject to change by the Legislature.

la.title: Special election, state Senate District 14
la.what: Special general election to fill one state Senate seat in the East Baton Rouge area.
la.note: Only voters in that district. Follows the Dec 12 special primary. Dates are subject to change by the Legislature.

la.title: Special primary, state House District 77
la.what: Special primary to fill one state House seat in St. Tammany Parish.
la.note: Only voters in that district. Dates are subject to change by the Legislature.

la.title: Special general election, state House District 77
la.what: Special general election for the same St. Tammany Parish state House seat.
la.note: Only voters in that district. Dates are subject to change by the Legislature.

la.title: Spring party primary and city primary
la.what: State school board (BESE) party primaries and primaries for city and town offices that are on the ballot.
la.note: Only voters in districts and towns that have a race. Dates are subject to change by the Legislature.

la.title: Spring second party primary and city general election
la.what: Second round for the school board party primaries, plus the general election for city and town offices.
la.note: Only voters in places with a race. Dates are subject to change by the Legislature.

la.title: Governor and statewide primary
la.what: Open primary for governor and other statewide offices, plus state legislature seats and the general election for the state school board (BESE).
la.note: The official calendar says this date was moved up one week under state law (R.S. 18:402). Dates are subject to change by the Legislature.

la.title: Governor and statewide general election
la.what: Runoff for the governor and other statewide or legislative races where nobody won a majority on Oct 9.
la.note: Only needed for races without a majority winner. Dates are subject to change by the Legislature.

me.title: Statewide ballot questions (if any)
me.what: Maine votes on statewide ballot questions (citizen petitions, bond issues, or state law changes) on the Tuesday after the first Monday in November in odd years, when any have qualified.
me.note: The Secretary of State had not posted a 2027 question list as of Oct 26, 2026. The date comes from Maine's regular schedule, so confirm after the Legislature finishes its 2027 session. Maine allows same-day voter registration at the town office.

me.title: Town and city elections
me.what: Voters choose local officials and vote on local budgets and questions at town meetings or city elections.
me.note: Maine's Secretary of State says it does not run local elections; each town sets its own date under its charter or state law.

md.title: City and town elections
md.what: Some Maryland cities and towns elect mayors and councils in 2027 on dates they choose, for example in spring or fall.
md.note: Maryland has no statewide election in 2027, and no state special election was listed as of Oct 26, 2026. Dates differ by town; the State Board of Elections keeps a municipal list.

ma.title: City and town elections
ma.what: Many Massachusetts cities (for example, Boston) hold elections for mayor and city council in the fall of odd years; towns hold town elections on dates they pick.
ma.note: No statewide election in 2027, and no special state election was on the Secretary of the Commonwealth's list as of Oct 26, 2026. Local dates differ by city and town.

mi.title: May regular election date
mi.what: Local ballot questions, such as school bonds and tax measures, and some local offices where one is scheduled.
mi.note: Michigan law only allows elections on set dates: the Tuesday after the first Monday in May, August and November. Computed from MCL 168.641; the vote only happens where something is on the local ballot.

mi.title: August regular election date
mi.what: Primaries for local offices and local ballot questions where a community has one.
mi.note: Computed from MCL 168.641 (Tuesday after the first Monday in August). Only communities with something on the ballot vote.

mi.title: November regular election date
mi.what: Mayor, city council, township and school board races and local ballot questions in communities that elect in odd years.
mi.note: Computed from MCL 168.641 (Tuesday after the first Monday in November). There are no statewide offices in 2027. I could not confirm whether any state special election has been called.

mn.title: Township elections
mn.what: Voters in townships choose township officials and vote on township questions.
mn.note: Listed on the Secretary of State's election calendar. Only townships that hold their election in March.

mn.title: State primary date (local primaries only)
mn.what: In 2027 this is a primary for city and school district offices that have too many candidates.
mn.note: Only places with a primary on the ballot vote. The registration date is 21 days before, the same rule as in 2026.

mn.title: General election (local)
mn.what: City and school district races and local ballot questions in places that elect in odd years. No statewide offices in 2027.
mn.note: Registration date is computed as 21 days before; Minnesota also allows same-day registration at the polls.

ms.title: General election runoff (December)
ms.what: Second round for judge and school board races, and some special elections, where nobody won a majority on Nov 3.
ms.note: Only needed if a race has no majority winner.

ms.title: Primary election
ms.what: Party primaries for governor, other statewide offices, the state legislature, and many county offices.
ms.note: From the Secretary of State's 2026-2027 calendar, which says dates can change. The registration deadline is about 30 days before; not yet posted for 2027.

ms.title: Primary runoff
ms.what: Second round for any primary race where nobody won a majority on Aug 3.
ms.note: Only needed for races without a majority winner.

ms.title: General election
ms.what: Voters choose the governor and other statewide officials, state legislators, and county officials.
ms.note: The registration deadline is about 30 days before; the Secretary of State had not posted the exact 2027 date.

ms.title: General election runoff
ms.what: Second round for judge, school board or special races where nobody won a majority on Nov 2.
ms.note: Only needed if a race has no majority winner.

mo.title: Bond election day
mo.what: Cities, school districts and other local groups can ask voters to approve bonds (borrowing money). Nothing else can be on this ballot.
mo.note: Only places that called a bond vote.

mo.title: Charter city and county election day
mo.what: Only charter cities and charter counties may hold elections on this date, per their local charter.
mo.note: Only places whose charter uses this date.

mo.title: General municipal election
mo.what: Voters choose city and town officials and school board members, and vote on local questions.

mo.title: August election date
mo.what: An election date available to local governments and special districts for votes and ballot questions.
mo.note: Only places that called an election.

mo.title: November election date
mo.what: An election date available to local governments and special districts for votes and ballot questions. No statewide offices in 2027.
mo.note: Only places that called an election.

mt.title: School district election
mt.what: Voters choose school trustees and vote on school levies and bonds in districts that hold an election.
mt.note: State law (20-20-105 MCA) sets the regular school election day as the first Tuesday after the first Monday in May. The Secretary of State has not yet posted a 2027 calendar.

mt.title: City and town primary (if needed)
mt.what: Primary for mayors and city or town council seats where there are too many candidates.
mt.note: State law (13-1-107 MCA) puts it on the Tuesday following the second Monday in September in odd years. Only held if required. Computed date.

mt.title: City and town general election
mt.what: Voters choose mayors and city or town council members and vote on local questions. No statewide offices in 2027.
mt.note: State law (13-1-104 MCA) holds municipal elections on general election day in odd years. Computed date; registration deadline not yet posted.

ne.title: City and village elections
ne.what: Some Nebraska cities, including Omaha and Lincoln, vote on mayors and city councils in the spring of odd-numbered years; school and other local districts also have their own dates.
ne.note: Nebraska has no statewide election in 2027. Local dates differ by city and are set by the county election office. I did not find an official statewide list of 2027 local dates.

nh.title: Town elections
nh.what: Voters in towns choose local officials and school board members and vote on local questions (many towns also hold town meeting).
nh.note: This is the standard town election date on the state political calendar. The calendar also lists an alternate town election on May 11, 2027, and towns with the SB2 system may vote on Mar 9, Apr 13 or May 11. New Hampshire allows same-day registration.

nj.title: Primary election
nj.what: Democratic and Republican voters pick their candidates for the state Senate and General Assembly, plus county and local offices.
nj.note: Computed: New Jersey law (N.J.S.A. 19:2-1) puts the primary on the Tuesday after the first Monday in June; the 2026 official timeline confirms the rule. The Division of Elections had not posted a 2027 timeline.

nj.title: General election
nj.what: Voters choose all state Senate and General Assembly seats, plus county and local offices and any ballot questions.
nj.note: Computed from state law (first Tuesday after the first Monday in November). The registration deadline is 21 days before.

nm.title: Regular local election
nm.what: Voters choose members of local governing bodies such as school boards, community colleges and special districts, and vote on local questions. No statewide offices in 2027.
nm.note: The Secretary of State says the Regular Local Election is held every November of odd years; the day is computed as the Tuesday after the first Monday. Registration deadline computed as 28 days before.

ny.title: Primary election (local offices)
ny.what: Party primaries for the local offices that are on the ballot in 2027, such as some county, city, town and judge seats.
ny.note: Computed: state law makes the fourth Tuesday in June the primary day. No statewide offices are up in 2027. The Board of Elections had not posted a 2027 calendar. Registration deadline computed as 10 days before.

ny.title: General election (local offices)
ny.what: Local offices on the ballot in 2027 (some county, city, town and court seats) and any ballot questions. No governor or legislature races in 2027.
ny.note: Computed: general election is the Tuesday after the first Monday in November. A 2023 law moved many local races to even years, so fewer places vote in 2027. Registration deadline computed as 10 days before.

nc.title: Municipal elections
nc.what: Cities and towns that use a one-round vote choose mayors and councils. Many towns with party or two-round systems hold earlier primaries in September or October.
nc.note: Computed from G.S. 163-279 (Tuesday after the first Monday in November for one-round nonpartisan elections); each town's charter sets its method. No statewide offices in 2027. Registration deadline computed as 25 days before, as in 2026.

nd.title: Local and special elections (dates vary)
nd.what: Cities, school districts and other local groups can hold special votes (like a tax or bond question) on dates they choose. The state can also call a special election to fill a vacancy.
nd.note: North Dakota has no regular statewide election in 2027. City and school races are decided at the June primary in even-numbered years (next one is June 2028), and the state website says local groups may run their own special elections on their own dates. North Dakota does not require voter registration, so there is no registration deadline.

oh.title: Municipal and school primary election
oh.what: A primary to narrow down candidates for city, village, township and school board jobs, in places that use primaries. Some local tax and bond questions can also appear.
oh.note: The 30th day before the election is a Sunday, so the official calendar moves the deadline to Monday April 5. Only places with more candidates than open seats hold a primary, and a few charter cities use different dates.

oh.title: August special election
oh.what: A special election date for a limited set of local issues. It only happens if a local group qualifies for it.
oh.note: Listed on the official 2027 calendar. Ohio law now limits what can go on August ballots, so many voters will not have anything to vote on this day. The deadline moves from July 4 (a Sunday) to July 6 on the official calendar.

oh.title: General election (city, township and school board)
oh.what: Voters choose mayors, city and village councils, township officials and school board members, and decide local tax and bond questions. There are no state or federal offices on the ballot in odd years.
oh.note: The 30th day before the election is a Sunday, so the official calendar moves the deadline to Monday October 4.

ok.title: Board of Education primary and special elections
ok.what: A primary for local school board seats, plus any special primaries that have been called, such as for a county judge seat.
ok.note: Early voting is Feb. 4-5. Only places with a race on the ballot hold an election.

ok.title: Board of Education general and special elections
ok.what: The main vote for local school board seats, plus any special general elections that have been called.

ok.title: Special elections (only if called)
ok.what: A day set aside for special elections, such as local tax or bond questions. Nothing is on the ballot unless a local group or the state calls one.
ok.note: Early voting is June 10-11. The state also reserves other dates (Jan. 12, Mar. 2, May 4, July 13, Sept. 14, Oct. 5, Dec. 14) only to fill empty state or federal offices.

ok.title: Special elections (only if called)
ok.what: A day set aside for special elections, such as local tax or bond questions. Nothing is on the ballot unless one is called.

ok.title: Special elections (only if called)
ok.what: A day set aside for special elections, such as local tax or bond questions. Nothing is on the ballot unless one is called.
ok.note: Early voting is Oct. 28-29. The state lists this date as special elections only, not a regular general election.

or.title: March local election date (only if called)
or.what: A date local governments can use for votes on local measures. Nothing is on the ballot unless a city, county or district puts something there.
or.note: Listed on the state's 2027 local elections calendar. Oregon registration closes 21 days before an election (about Feb. 16), but that exact date is not yet published, so it is not given here.

or.title: May district election
or.what: The regular election for many local district boards (such as school, fire, water and park districts) and for local measures.
or.note: Listed on the state's 2027 local elections calendar; state law puts the May election on the third Tuesday of May. Registration closes 21 days before (about April 27), but that exact date is not yet published.

or.title: August local election date (only if called)
or.what: A date local governments can use for votes on local measures. Nothing is on the ballot unless a local government calls one.
or.note: Listed on the state's 2027 local elections calendar. Registration closes 21 days before (about Aug. 3), but that exact date is not yet published.

or.title: November local election
or.what: Local measures and some city or district races. There are no state or federal offices on the ballot in odd years.
or.note: Listed on the state's 2027 local elections calendar. Registration closes 21 days before (about Oct. 12), but that exact date is not yet published.

pa.title: Municipal primary
pa.what: A primary to pick party candidates for local jobs such as mayor, city or borough council, school board, township supervisor and county offices.
pa.note: Mail-in ballot request deadline is May 11. The state says dates can change without notice.

pa.title: Municipal election
pa.what: Voters choose local officials such as mayors, councils, school boards, and township and county offices. There are no federal or governor races in odd years.
pa.note: Mail-in ballot request deadline is Oct. 26. The state's special elections page listed no upcoming special elections on Oct. 26, 2026; new ones can be called at any time if a seat opens.

ri.title: Special and local elections (as needed)
ri.what: Rhode Island has no regular statewide election in 2027. A special election is held only if a seat opens up or a town or city calls a vote on a local question.
ri.note: On Oct. 26, 2026 the state's Upcoming Elections page listed only the Nov. 3, 2026 general election, with no 2027 dates. Statewide primaries and general elections come back in 2028.

sc.title: Municipal and special elections (dates vary by town)
sc.what: Each town or city sets its own election date, so some places vote in 2027 and some do not. Special elections to fill an empty seat can also be called at any time.
sc.note: South Carolina has more than 270 towns and cities, and the state says each one is responsible for setting its own election date. The state's Upcoming Elections page is updated every two weeks and lists each local election.

sd.title: City and school elections (June 8 or Nov. 2, set locally)
sd.what: Every city and school district holds an election each year for local officers. Each one picks which of the two allowed days to use.
sd.note: State law (SDCL 9-13-1 and 13-7-10) allows these elections only on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in June or in November. Computed for 2027, that is Tuesday June 8 or Tuesday November 2. Each city or school board picks its date by a January deadline, so ask your city or school district which one applies.

tn.title: City and special elections (dates vary)
tn.what: Tennessee has no regular statewide election in 2027. Some cities hold their own city elections in odd years, and special elections can be called to fill an empty seat.
tn.note: State and county elections happen in even years. A state advisory commission report says some cities, including Nashville, use odd-year dates (Nashville's past city elections were on the first Thursday of August). I could not find a 2027 statewide calendar from the Secretary of State, so confirm with your county election commission.

tx.title: Local runoff election
tx.what: A second round for city, school district and other local races from the Nov. 3, 2026 election where nobody won a majority.
tx.note: The Secretary of State set this Saturday date for local runoffs. Early voting is Nov. 30 to Dec. 8. It only happens in places with a runoff.

tx.title: May uniform election date
tx.what: Cities, school districts and other local groups elect their leaders and vote on local bonds and tax questions.
tx.note: The Secretary of State's calendar names May 1, 2027 as a uniform election date. Texas registration closes 30 days before an election (about April 1), but the exact date is not yet published. Runoffs, if needed, are set later by the state.

tx.title: November uniform election date
tx.what: Cities, school districts and other local groups hold elections, and any state constitutional amendments the Legislature approves in 2027 appear on this ballot.
tx.note: The Secretary of State's calendar names Nov. 2, 2027 as a uniform election date. Whether there are statewide amendments will not be known until after the 2027 legislative session. Registration closes 30 days before (about Oct. 4, since the 30th day is a Sunday), but the exact date is not yet published.

ut.title: Municipal primary (only where needed)
ut.what: A primary to narrow down candidates for city and town offices, held only in cities with more candidates than allowed on the general ballot.
ut.note: Computed from state law: the municipal primary is the second Tuesday after the first Monday in August (the 2025 one was Aug. 12). Many towns skip it. Utah's registration deadline for the 2026 general election was 11 days before the election, so expect about July 30, but the 2027 date is not yet published.

ut.title: Municipal general election
ut.what: Voters choose mayors and city or town council members, and decide local questions. There are no state or federal offices on the ballot in odd years.
ut.note: Computed from state law: the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of an odd-numbered year. Registration closes about 11 days before (around Oct. 22), but the exact date is not yet published.

vt.title: Town Meeting Day
vt.what: Towns and school districts elect local officers and vote on town and school budgets and local questions, in person or by ballot.
vt.note: Computed from state law: annual town meeting is the first Tuesday of March. A town may start its meeting earlier, in the three days before, and some towns vote by paper ballot all day. Vermont lets people register up to and including election day, so no earlier deadline is listed.

va.title: Special election: Town of Purcellville (Loudoun County)
va.what: A special election to fill a seat on the Purcellville Town Council.
va.note: Only voters in that town are affected.

va.title: Special election: Chancellor District, Spotsylvania County
va.what: A special election to fill a seat on the county Board of Supervisors for the Chancellor District.
va.note: Only voters in that district are affected.

va.title: Special election: sales tax question, Washington County
va.what: A local vote on a sales tax question in Washington County.
va.note: Only voters in that county are affected.

va.title: Primary election (if held)
va.what: A primary where parties pick their candidates for the November 2027 State Senate, House of Delegates and local offices.
va.note: The state's five-year calendar lists June 15 for 2027, but only for races where a party chooses to hold a primary. Virginia moved the 2026 primary to August 4 by a special law, so this date could also change. Virginia registration closes 11 days before an election (about June 4), but the exact date is not yet published.

va.title: General election
va.what: Voters choose all of the State Senate and House of Delegates, plus local offices like boards of supervisors, school boards, sheriffs and some city and town councils.
va.note: Date is on the state's five-year election calendar. Virginia registration closes 11 days before an election (about Oct. 22), with same-day registration by provisional ballot after that, but the exact 2027 date is not yet published.

wa.title: February special election
wa.what: A date local governments (schools, cities, fire and other districts) can use for votes on levies and other local questions.
wa.note: Feb. 1 is the deadline to register online or by mail. In-person registration is allowed up to 8 pm on election day. Only places with a measure on the ballot vote.

wa.title: April special election
wa.what: A date local governments can use for votes on levies, bonds and other local questions.
wa.note: April 19 is the deadline to register online or by mail; in-person registration is allowed up to election day. Only places with a measure on the ballot vote.

wa.title: Primary election
wa.what: A primary that narrows the field for city, school board and other local races where more than two people are running.
wa.note: July 26 is the deadline to register online or by mail; in-person registration is allowed up to election day. Only places with races that need a primary vote.

wa.title: General election
wa.what: Voters choose local officials such as city councils, school boards and port and fire commissioners, and vote on local measures. The state can also add statewide measures.
wa.note: Oct. 25 is the deadline to register online or by mail; in-person registration is allowed up to election day.

wv.title: Municipal elections (date set by each city or town)
wv.what: Some cities and towns elect mayors and councils in 2027. Each one sets its own date.
wv.note: The state's municipal guide says the statutory general election day for towns is the second Tuesday in June, which in 2027 is June 8, but towns can use other dates and many used different days in 2026 (for example June 2 and June 9). The state lists the year's municipal elections each spring. West Virginia registration closes 21 days before an election.

wi.title: Spring primary
wi.what: A primary for nonpartisan races (judges and local offices) that have more than two candidates, to narrow the list for April.
wi.note: State law sets this as the third Tuesday in February. It is only held if a race has more than two candidates. Online and mail registration closes the third Wednesday before the election (Jan. 27); after that people can register in person at the clerk's office or on election day.

wi.title: Spring election
wi.what: Voters choose judges and local officials (such as school boards, mayors and county boards) and may vote on local questions.
wi.note: State law sets this as the first Tuesday in April, and the Elections Commission's 2027 calendar lists April 6. Online and mail registration closes Wednesday March 17; after that people can register in person at the clerk's office or on election day.

wy.title: Town, bond and special elections (dates vary)
wy.what: Some towns hold elections in May, and local groups can hold votes on bonds in May or November. Special elections can also be called to fill an empty seat.
wy.note: Wyoming law (W.S. 22-2-104) allows a May town election every two years on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in May (May 4, 2027, if your town is on that cycle), and bond elections on that day or the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November (Nov. 2, 2027). There is no regular statewide election in 2027.

al.text: Alabama state law puts the presidential primary on the first Tuesday in March in presidential years, which is March 7, 2028.

az.text: Arizona law puts the presidential preference election on the Tuesday after March 15 in presidential years, which is March 21, 2028. The Governor can move it by proclamation.

ar.text: Arkansas law puts the presidential-year primary on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in March, which is March 7, 2028.

ca.text: California holds its presidential primary on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in March in presidential years, which is March 7, 2028.

ct.text: Connecticut law puts presidential primaries on the first Tuesday in April of presidential years, which is April 4, 2028. A party only holds one in a town if it has two or more candidates.

de.text: Delaware law puts the presidential primary on the fourth Tuesday in April of presidential years, which is April 25, 2028. A party can opt out.

dc.text: D.C. law puts the presidential primary on the first Tuesday in June of presidential years, which is June 6, 2028.

fl.text: Florida's next presidential preference primary is March 21, 2028 (the third Tuesday in March). It is closed, so only voters registered with a party can take part.

il.text: Illinois' general primary, which includes the presidential primary, is on the third Tuesday in March of even years, which is March 21, 2028.

in.text: Indiana's primary, which includes the presidential primary, is held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in May, which is May 2, 2028.

ky.text: Kentucky holds its presidential primary on the same day as its regular May primary, the first Tuesday after the third Monday in May. The date is worked out from state law (KRS 118.025 and 118.561), not yet posted on a published 2028 calendar.

la.text: Louisiana holds its presidential preference primary on the last Saturday in March; party members of the two large parties vote.

me.text: Maine's presidential primary is held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in March, if a party has a contested race for its nominee. Date is worked out from state law (21-A MRSA section 441); the Secretary of State announces which parties qualify after Oct 1, 2027.

md.text: Under current state law, Maryland's presidential primary is the fourth Tuesday in April of a presidential year. The date comes from state law (Election Law section 8-201) and lawmakers moved it for 2024, so they could change it in 2027.

ma.text: Massachusetts holds presidential primaries on the first Tuesday in March of a presidential year. Date is computed from state law (Chapter 53, Section 28).

mi.text: Michigan holds its presidential primary on the fourth Tuesday in February of a presidential year. Date is computed from MCL 168.613a; lawmakers could still change it.

mn.text: Minnesota's presidential primary is on the first Tuesday in March of a presidential year.

ms.text: State law allows a party to hold a presidential preference primary on the second Tuesday in March of a presidential year. Date computed from Miss. Code 23-15-1081; the party chooses whether to hold it.

mt.text: Montana's primary is on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in June in even years, and presidential nominating contests use that date. Date is computed from state law (13-1-107 MCA).

ne.text: Nebraska's statewide primary, which includes the vote for presidential preference, is the first Tuesday after the second Monday in May of even years. Date computed from state law (Neb. Rev. Stat. 32-401); the Secretary of State posts the official 2028 calendar by Nov 1, 2027.

nv.text: Nevada's presidential preference primary is on the first Tuesday in February of a presidential year, unless a party has only one candidate. Date computed from state law (NRS 298.650); lawmakers meet in 2027 and could change it.

nj.text: New Jersey holds its presidential primary on the Tuesday after the first Monday in June of a presidential year. Date computed from the same state law; the state had not posted a 2028 timeline.

nm.text: New Mexico's presidential primary is held on the same day as its state primary, the first Tuesday after the first Monday in June. Date computed from state law (NMSA 1-15A-2 and 1-8-11); not yet posted by the Secretary of State.

nc.text: North Carolina holds its presidential primary on the Tuesday after the first Monday in March of a presidential year. Date computed from state law (G.S. 163-213.2); not yet published by the State Board.

oh.text: Ohio's presidential primary is scheduled for Tuesday, March 21, 2028.

ok.text: Oklahoma law puts the presidential primary on the first Tuesday in March, which is March 7, 2028.

or.text: Oregon's primary, which includes the presidential race, is on the third Tuesday in May, which is May 16, 2028.

pa.text: Pennsylvania's presidential primary is held on the fourth Tuesday of April, which is April 25, 2028.

ri.text: Rhode Island law holds the presidential primary on the fourth Tuesday in April every fourth year, which is April 25, 2028.

sd.text: South Dakota's primary, which includes the presidential race, is the first Tuesday after the first Monday in June, which is June 6, 2028.

tn.text: Tennessee law holds the presidential primary on the first Tuesday in March, which is March 7, 2028.

tx.text: The Texas Secretary of State says the 2028 presidential primary will be held on March 7, 2028.

ut.text: Utah law holds the presidential primary on the first Tuesday in March of a presidential election year, which is March 7, 2028.

vt.text: The Vermont Secretary of State lists the 2028 presidential primary for March 7, 2028.

va.text: Virginia's calendar lists a presidential primary on March 7, 2028, if the political parties choose to hold one.

wa.text: Washington law holds the presidential primary on the second Tuesday in March, which is March 14, 2028, unless a different date is set by Oct. 1, 2027.

wv.text: West Virginia holds its primary, which includes the presidential race, on the second Tuesday in May, which is May 9, 2028.

wi.text: Wisconsin holds its presidential preference vote on the spring election day, the first Tuesday in April, which is April 4, 2028.

localNote.al: Alabama does not run one statewide date for local elections each year; cities and counties set their own, and the Secretary of State lists them at sos.alabama.gov/alabama-votes/voter/upcoming-elections.
localNote.ak: Alaska towns, boroughs and school districts each set their own election dates (many use the first Tuesday in October, Anchorage uses the first Tuesday in April); check your city or borough clerk and elections.alaska.gov/calendar.
localNote.az: Arizona only lets local governments hold elections on a few set dates (March, May, July in even years, and November), but each city, town or school district chooses whether to use them; in 2027 only measures, not people, are voted on; the second-to-last Tuesday in July (July 20, 2027) is also an allowed date for measures; check your county elections office.
localNote.ar: Arkansas city and school dates mostly follow the March primary and November general election in even years; for special local elections check your county clerk or the Secretary of State at sos.arkansas.gov/elections.
localNote.ca: California law allows local elections only on a few set dates (March, April and June in some years, and November), but each city, school district or district decides whether to use them; check your county elections office. Special elections for vacancies in the legislature or Congress are called by the Governor as needed.
localNote.co: Colorado cities and towns each set their own municipal election dates (many use April of odd years) while school boards and special districts use the November odd-year "coordinated election"; check your county clerk.
localNote.ct: Connecticut sets municipal elections statewide for November of odd years (some towns pick May); check your town clerk or portal.ct.gov/sots.
localNote.de: Delaware school board elections are in May, but town and city elections follow each municipality's own calendar; see elections.delaware.gov/public/calendar/calendars.html.
localNote.dc: D.C. elects its mayor, Council and other offices in even-numbered years; special elections for vacancies and neighborhood commission (ANC) vacancies are called as needed, so check dcboe.org.
localNote.fl: Florida city and special district election dates vary; check your county Supervisor of Elections or the state's Local Elections Database.
localNote.ga: Georgia cities hold their elections in odd-numbered years, mostly in November, but exact schedules and which offices are up vary by city, so check your county elections office or mvp.sos.ga.gov.
localNote.hi: Hawaii's regular elections are statewide and held only in even-numbered years (primary in August, general in November); special elections are called only when certain seats open, so check elections.hawaii.gov.
localNote.id: Idaho lets local governments hold elections only on the third Tuesday in May and the November election date, so check your county clerk to see what is on your ballot.
localNote.il: Illinois sets the same local election days statewide (consolidated primary in February and consolidated election in April of odd years); check your county clerk or elections.il.gov for what is on your ballot.
localNote.in: Indiana holds city and town elections in odd-numbered years (primary in May, election in November); a few tiny towns and special-charter towns differ, so check your county election office.
localNote.ia: Iowa runs one set of city and school elections statewide in November of odd years (with an October primary in some cities); special elections to fill vacancies can be called on most Tuesdays, so check your county auditor.
localNote.ks: Kansas holds city and school elections in odd-numbered years in November (with an August primary if needed); check your county election office or sos.ks.gov.
localNote.ky: Kentucky's regular local offices (mayors, city councils, county offices) are on the even-year ballots; check your county clerk for special local votes.
localNote.la: Louisiana sets uniform election dates for the whole state; check the Secretary of State's election calendar or your parish registrar for what is on your ballot.
localNote.me: Maine's Secretary of State does not run town or city elections; ask your municipal clerk.
localNote.md: Maryland towns and cities set their own election dates; check your local board of elections or town hall.
localNote.ma: Each Massachusetts city or town sets its own election date; ask your city or town clerk.
localNote.mi: Michigan only allows elections on three set dates a year (May, August, November); your city or township clerk can say if your area has one.
localNote.mn: Minnesota special elections can only be held on certain dates; check the Secretary of State's special elections page or your county auditor (I could not load that page, so none are confirmed here).
localNote.ms: Mississippi's regular local offices are elected in the same statewide cycles; check your circuit clerk for special local votes.
localNote.mo: Missouri sets uniform election days (Feb, Mar, Apr, Aug, Nov), but each city, school or district decides whether to hold one; ask your local election authority. The state-run presidential primary was repealed in 2022 and a 2026 bill to bring it back did not pass, so 2028 has no state-set date yet.
localNote.mt: Montana sets school (May) and city (Sept/Nov) election days by state law, but only places with something to vote on hold elections; ask your county elections office.
localNote.ne: Local election dates in Nebraska vary by city and district; check your county election office.
localNote.nv: No regular Nevada elections were found between Nov 2026 and the 2028 presidential primary; any special election would be announced by the Secretary of State or your county clerk.
localNote.nh: Most New Hampshire towns vote on the second Tuesday of March; ask your town or city clerk for your date. The 2028 presidential primary date is set by the Secretary of State and had not been announced.
localNote.nj: Many New Jersey towns hold May or November nonpartisan elections; ask your county clerk or municipal clerk.
localNote.nm: New Mexico's Local Election Act uses one regular local election in November of odd years; municipal officers are elected in March of even years.
localNote.ny: Which local offices are on New York's 2027 ballot depends on your county and town; check your county board of elections.
localNote.nc: North Carolina cities and towns set their election method in their charters; check your county board of elections.
localNote.nd: North Dakota cities and school districts mostly vote at the June primary and November general election in even years; for a special vote, check your county auditor or the Secretary of State's special elections page.
localNote.oh: Ohio sets one statewide schedule for local elections (May primary and November general in odd years); check your county board of elections for what is on your ballot.
localNote.ok: Oklahoma cities and towns hold their own elections on the state's set dates (Feb, Apr, Aug, Nov); check your county election board to see which apply to you.
localNote.or: Oregon votes entirely by mail; your county elections office tells you which of the four statewide local election dates your city or district is using.
localNote.pa: Pennsylvania sets one statewide date for municipal primaries and elections; your county elections office has the list of races in your area.
localNote.ri: Rhode Island has no regular local election dates in odd years; check your city or town clerk or the state elections page for any special vote.
localNote.sc: South Carolina towns and cities choose their own election dates; look up yours on the Election Commission's Upcoming Elections page or ask your county elections office.
localNote.sd: South Dakota cities and school districts hold an election every year, either in June or November; your city finance office or school district tells you which day.
localNote.tn: Tennessee cities set some of their own election dates; check your county election commission for any 2027 city vote.
localNote.tx: Texas cities and districts must use one of the state's uniform election dates (first Saturday in May and first Tuesday after the first Monday in November); your county elections office lists what is on your ballot.
localNote.ut: Utah cities and towns use the state's set municipal dates; your county clerk tells you whether your city has a primary.
localNote.vt: Vermont towns vote on Town Meeting Day in March; each town clerk posts its own warning with the exact time, place and items.
localNote.va: Virginia's local offices are on the state's set schedule, but small special elections get added during the year; the Department of Elections' Upcoming Elections page lists them.
localNote.wa: Washington votes by mail, and local governments must use one of four set dates each year; your county elections office lists what is on your ballot.
localNote.wv: West Virginia towns pick their own election dates; ask your city or town recorder or clerk.
localNote.wi: Wisconsin local offices are mostly on the April spring election; your municipal clerk lists the races and questions in your area.
localNote.wy: Wyoming has no regular statewide election in 2027; ask your county clerk or town clerk whether your town is voting in May or has a bond question.
